classification_basis.reference: FAA Allocation Report: Remote Tower Systems for Non-Federal Applications, 2021-09-16, Table 8-1
classification_basis.method: Engineering candidate consequence classes only. No system safety assessment, probability allocation, external barrier credit, or DO-278A assurance level is assigned.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The named-proof runner records its pinned tool versions and rejects mismatched versions, source bindings or scoped loop diagnostics. Scoped loop presets accept only a registered complete identity family at the declared bounds. In fail-fast mode, the suite stops launching proofs after a non-passing result, reports its diagnostics, records remaining selected proofs as `NOT_RUN`, and cannot report an overall pass.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This checks requirement/test/proof links and trace reporting; it has no runtime aircraft-state or operator-output path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every `pub trait` (unrestricted `pub`, `unsafe` included) in core code is sealed, meaning one of its supertraits is reached through a module the crate declares non-public (`mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} }` and `pub trait T: sealed::Sealed`, or `Sealed` imported through that module), or is listed in `tools/oa-trace/core-callbacks-allowlist.txt` as `crate file.rs::TraitName reason`. A `pub use` of the sealing trait and a blanket `impl<X> sealed::Sealed for X` un-seal it and fail. The sealing trait itself, `pub(crate)` and private traits and test-only ones are not listed.

Private and `pub(crate)` items may carry any bound, a type parameter with no bound is not checked; the header of an `impl` is OA-TRC-252. A bound is read through parentheses, `?` and `for<..>`; one that still has no name (anything but `?Sized` or a lifetime) fails.

Private and `pub(crate)` items, and bodies, may use closures, `dyn` and fn pointers.

Every use in the real core crates is migrated.

The live loop decides each turn by pure functions: it stops only when stopping, the stop condition holds and no input or drain is owed; it services when input or a drain is owed, else it receives. A retryable push refusal defers with no drain pending, a retryable drain refusal defers with a drain pending, and a refusal a fresh allowance cannot satisfy, a counter overflow, or a push that takes no bytes cancels the stream with an error naming the refusal, the reader-buffer bytes, the unpushed input bytes and the deferral count.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This deletes only verified expired archive segments under explicit ownership/identity checks; it does not alter the live feed path or operational track/alert state. Its source clause preserves the residual concurrent-writer limitation.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Retention cleanup runs before the storage-cap decision and removes only canonical expired feed segments with a V2 owner marker bound to the segment device/inode and a matching closed receipt. The path and opened regular-file descriptor identities are checked before deletion; a replacement inode, unmarked file, malformed marker, non-regular file or symlink is preserved. The cleanup is bounded by the recorder's directory-entry limit. These sidecars are not cryptographic authentication: retention assumes the recording directory is not concurrently modified by an untrusted writer, and path-based unlink retains a narrow TOCTOU window against a concurrent same-directory replacement.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds generic compressed-input decoding and replay framing; it does not decide track, flight, or alert state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Never panics and always round-trips for chunk sizes from 1 byte upward (1, 7, 258, 4097, ...), irregular chunking and interspersed flushes, empty writes, and finish or flush with nothing written.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds generic compressed-input decoding and replay framing; it does not decide track, flight, or alert state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Output is a pure function of input, level and write boundaries (no clock, no randomness); a compressor is reusable after `finish` or `reset` with identical output, and allocates only in `new`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds generic compressed-input decoding and replay framing; it does not decide track, flight, or alert state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An error returned by the output closure is returned unchanged by `write`, `flush` and `finish`; the compressor works again after `reset`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every message of the real TBFM sample (`OPENATCA_SCDS`, directories named `tbfm*`) decodes with no reject and no unknown path; the test reports messages, rows and rejects by reason, field errors by field, distinct flights, GUFIs, airports and meter fixes, and throughput, which must be at least 20,000 messages per second (parse and decode, one thread, release builds); it skips when the variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Against an airspace snapshot of one ARTCC (`OPENATCA_SNAPSHOT`) the real rows' meter fixes and airports are resolved to model points, and the distinct identifiers and rows that resolve are reported for all centres and for the model's own centre; the test skips when either variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The cross-check resolves a meter fix to a model fix, navaid or terminal waypoint and an airport to a model airport by its identifier or alternate identifier (never to a runway threshold), counts distinct identifiers and rows per role and per scope (all centres, the model's own centre) and lists the identifiers that do not resolve.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `spd` carries its unit with the value (`spd_unit`: none, knots, Mach, unknown), read from the value's form because the feed has no marker: `ddd.d` is knots, `d.dd` is Mach (all jets in the recorded sample), any other form is stored with the unknown unit and counted (`unknown_units`); units are never mixed in a column without it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A schedule flag with a word other than `YES` or `NO` keeps the flight, stores the flag as unknown and is counted (`unknown_words`); an unknown change type still refuses the flight. `msgId` (ten digits) is stored as `u64`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Values are trimmed of outer whitespace; the site-adapted labels (`gat`, `cfg`, `scn`, `cat`) may hold interior spaces (printable ASCII), identifiers and fixes may not. The TBFM schema is not in the repository, so that labels allow spaces is a decision, not a confirmed rule.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every message of the real TFMS sample (`OPENATCA_SCDS`, directories named `tfms*`) decodes with no reject and no unknown path; the test reports messages, rows by type, rejects by reason, field errors by field, distinct flights and throughput, which must be at least 20,000 messages per second (parse and decode, one thread, release builds); it skips when the variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Against the real SFDPS sample, TFMS flights are linked by GUFI and the overlap is reported as found; no TFMS GUFI equals an SFDPS GUFI and the two matching routes never name different flights; the test skips when the variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Counters over many documents (accepted, messages, rows by kind, rejects by reason, field errors by field, unknown and ignored paths) are folded by a free function.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The linkage matches a TFMS flight to the SFDPS flights by its GUFI (equal to the SFDPS flight plan identifier) and, when it has no GUFI, by aircraft identification plus departure plus arrival, and cross-checks flights found both ways.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is empirical sample or coverage diagnostics rather than the message-to-state mapping used by an operational function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The linkage report counts, as found, the flights with and without a GUFI, UUID-shaped GUFIs, keys that name more than one SFDPS flight and empty inputs.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The flight table is a struct-of-arrays of fixed capacity (default 32,768 flights) allocated once at construction; bad settings (capacity 0 or above 2^24, a non-positive age limit or sweep spacing) are errors. Its key indexes are sized to at least twice the capacity, so the load never exceeds 1/2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An SFDPS row, applied with the replay time as an argument, fills the flight's identity (callsign, computer id, departure, arrival, aircraft type, flight-plan id), last position (latitude, longitude, altitude, ground speed, track velocity), position time, last-update time, last source and controlling unit, and counts the update.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A position older than the flight's last position time never overwrites it: the row's position fields are dropped and the row is counted as out of order (per flight and in total), while its other fields still apply, with the exceptions of OA-RPL-201. An equal or newer position applies. A row without a usable position (absent or malformed) is never out of order, and leaves the position time as it was (OA-RPL-200).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Identity fields fill when empty and confirm when equal; a different non-empty callsign, departure, arrival or aircraft type is a counted field conflict and the held value is kept. The computer id is not identity (each centre assigns its own) and takes the latest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TBFM row links to the flight whose flight-plan identifier equals the row's `gufi` attribute (the TBFM `gufi` is the SFDPS `flightPlan@identifier`, not the SFDPS GUFI). A `gufi` matching no flight creates a TBFM-first flight, which takes its real GUFI when SFDPS reports the same flight plan; linked, created and promoted rows are counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TBFM row with no `gufi` links through the `(centre, tmaId)` pair, held in a second fixed-size index; a row that matches nothing is counted as unlinked and applies nothing. The same `tmaId` from another centre is another key.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TBFM rows set the metering columns: meter fix, ETA at the meter fix, STA (the scheduling-fix time where the feed has no meter-fix time), runway and the frozen flag (`sfz`). A TBFM row older than the flight's last TBFM message time is refused whole and counted as out of order.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TBFM `DEL` change type, on the `air` or on the `mrp` section, clears the metering columns and the frozen flag. It does not delete the flight, and metering can start again.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight is evicted only when its last update is more than its age limit (default 30 minutes, configurable, for a flight with no status seen; see OA-RPL-067 for the others) older than the replay time, at a sweep that runs on a fixed cadence of replay time (multiples of the sweep spacing, default one minute). Exactly the limit is not older than it. Nothing is evicted between sweeps.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A sweep visits slots in slot order and returns the evicted slots to a free stack, so slot reuse is deterministic; eviction removes the flight from every index.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A full table refuses a new flight (from either feed) and counts it; it never evicts early to make room. Existing flights keep updating, and the refused flight is admitted once a sweep has freed a slot (INTERFACES IF-R1).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The state hash is SHA-256 over a canonical serialisation iterating live flights in GUFI order, so it does not depend on insertion history: shuffled application of commuting updates gives the same hash.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The state hash does not depend on slot assignment or eviction history, and changes when any column changes; an empty table's hash does not depend on capacity.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The open-addressing index (linear probing, backward-shift deletion) agrees with a model under random inserts and removes, including with a degenerate hash that forces long probe runs; it refuses past load 1/2; its hash functions are fixed, unkeyed, deterministic functions of the key (not adversarial-robust, and bounded by the index length per operation).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The flight table allocates nothing after construction: every column and index keeps its address and capacity through applying, refusing, sweeping and evicting.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The pipeline takes replay time from each frame's `recv_unix_ns` and records a checkpoint (replay time, frames, rows applied, flights live, state hash) at the first frame at or after each multiple of the checkpoint spacing (default 10 s).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every parse, decode and apply failure is counted under its own kind (XML, unsupported root, bad GUFI, bad timestamp, malformed field, TBFM field, and the rest); REJECT and STATUS frames are counted and not decoded. Nothing is silently skipped.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A frame earlier than one already seen, by no more than the clock's step tolerance (10 minutes), does not move replay time back and is counted as a time regression; a larger difference follows OA-RPL-061 to OA-RPL-063.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Replaying the same recordings twice, or with the input read in any chunking (1 byte to 16 MiB), or with the streams named in another order, gives identical checkpoints, counters and final state hash.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A `.oaf.gz` recording replays identically to its raw `.oaf` (chosen by the file's first bytes); a gzip file cut short is counted and its frames up to the cut replay.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Recordings are read as streams and merged with a fixed-capacity min-heap, one head frame per stream, ordered by `(recv_unix_ns, feed kind, seq, stream index, byte offset)`: a total order, equal to a global sort of the same frames whenever each stream is in receive order. Memory is bounded by the number of streams times a fixed per-stream buffer, not by the input length (peak resident memory on the real recordings is reported by the binary's `timing` line).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Corrupted recordings (every single-byte flip, truncations, random garbage and damage) and corrupted XML payloads never panic; a damaged frame leaves a count, and a cut inside a frame is a counted truncation.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The `oa-replay` command line gives each file the feed kind of the flag that names it, sets the checkpoint spacing, age limit, sweep spacing and capacity, and rejects missing, zero, non-numeric and unknown arguments.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: In normal mode the `oa-replay` binary prints the checkpoints and a final summary (frames and rows per feed, TBFM linking, table totals, errors by kind, flights live and the final state hash); checkpoints are printed as they are recorded; a progress line (replay time, frames per second, replay-time to wall-time ratio, resident memory) goes to stderr every N minutes of replay time (default 10); every stdout line except the `timing` line is identical from run to run, whatever the flag order or read size; exit status is 2 for usage errors and 1 for an unreadable file.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Opt-in offline replay verification takes a positive admitted-frame count, an ordered-input digest and a replay-state digest from an independent witness. The prefix flag checks its exact admitted-frame boundary. The terminal flag checks the final count and both digests, including when a recording ends cleanly at the wrong boundary. Either flag suppresses intermediate checkpoints and withholds the final summary on a mismatch or a partial replay. A bridge `REJECT` marker is counted and makes the replay partial. A partial replay that reaches the final verification check reports aggregate blocker counts on standard error. The optional settings precondition verifies a separate versioned digest of the effective replay settings and ordered logical feed streams before any recording path is used.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Replaying the real SCDS recordings under `OPENATCA_REC` (SFDPS and TBFM) twice and with another read size gives identical checkpoints and the same final state hash, with no frame, gzip or clock error and TBFM rows linked to SFDPS flights (skipped if unset). The final hash equals that of the earlier all-in-memory replay.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The canonical serialisation of a fixed table state has a pinned golden hash, so a change of the serialisation or of what the state holds is a deliberate, visible edit.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This checks real-message sample compatibility and does not specify an active operational consumer.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every real FNS message of the local sample (`OPENATCA_SCDS`, directories named `fns*`) decodes with no rejection, no field error and no unknown path; the test reports messages, rows, rejections by reason, field errors by field, feature kinds, rows with geometry and throughput, which must be at least 20,000 messages per second (parse and decode, one thread, release builds); it skips when the variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This checks real-message sample compatibility and does not specify an active operational consumer.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Against an airspace snapshot of one ARTCC (`OPENATCA_SNAPSHOT`) the real rows' locations, airports, runways and navaids are resolved to model entries, and the polygons are tested against the model's ARTCC boundary; the distinct identifiers and rows that resolve are reported for all rows and for the model's own FIR; the test skips when either variable is unset.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ADS-B aircraft table keeps, per address (the 24-bit address, with the non-ICAO bit making a separate key), the latest report (time, latitude, longitude, barometric altitude, ground speed, track, flags, source type) and counts; callsign, squawk, category and the quality fields (NIC, NACp, NACv, SIL, SIL type, version, GVA, SDA) are carried forward from reports that have them.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ADS-B table is a struct-of-arrays of fixed capacity (65,536 aircraft) allocated once; a new address when it is full is refused and counted (per table and per feed), known aircraft keep updating, and no column moves or grows. Aircraft not heard for a while are freed (OA-RPL-065).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An ADS-B report older than the aircraft's held report is refused whole and counted (per aircraft, in total and per feed); an equal time applies.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ADS-B table is part of the replay state hash (`replay_hash`, used by every checkpoint and the final hash) in address order, so the hash does not depend on the order aircraft were first seen, and changes with any column or count.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Until an ADS-B frame has been fed the replay hash equals the flight-table hash, so the checkpoints and final hash of every replay without ADS-B are unchanged (pinned to the value the code gave before ADS-B existed).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An ADS-B payload whose header or length `oa_adsb::decode_payload_lenient` refuses (length, magic, layout, too many records) is counted under its own error kind and applies none of its reports; no corruption of a payload panics.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: ADS-B is a feed kind of its own that sorts after TFMS and FNS in the merge key, so at an equal receive time SWIM frames come first and ADS-B last, whatever order the streams were named in; the merged order is still the global sort of the total key (OA-RPL-021).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A mixed SFDPS, TBFM and ADS-B replay of hand-made recordings gives the same checkpoints, counters and final hash in every stream order and read size, with the right frame, row, aircraft and error counts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--adsb <file>` and `--adsb-dir <dir>` give a file or a directory of rotated recordings the ADS-B feed kind; the binary prints the ADS-B feed line, an `adsb` table line and the errors, identical run to run and across read sizes and rotation.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Replaying a real ADS-B clip written by `oa-adsb-clip` (`OPENATCA_ADSB_CLIP`) twice and with another read size gives identical checkpoints and final hash, with no error and no refused aircraft (skipped if unset).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An `oa-replay` merge of a one-second-frame ADS-B clip and a SWIM feed gives the frames in receive-time order, interleaved at about one-second granularity.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The TFMS flight table keeps, per flight reference, the latest value of each estimate and time the messages carried (estimated and actual departure and arrival, original, runway, gate, fix and coordination times, estimate flags and types, status), leaving a value alone when a later row lacks it; identity (acid, departure, arrival, identifier) fills an empty column and a disagreement is counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TFMS flight row older (by `sourceTimeStamp`) than the flight's latest is refused whole and counted; an equal time applies.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TFMS flight links to the SFDPS flight whose flight-plan identifier equals its identifier, or, with no identifier, to the single SFDPS flight with its acid, departure and arrival; an ambiguous key and an identifier that matches nothing leave it unlinked; the link is the SFDPS GUFI, retried while unlinked (the identifier every row, the acid key on the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th ... row) and counted by method.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TFMS programme rows (restrictions, advisories, FCA/FEA, airport configurations) keep one row per programme key with the latest row, count rows by program type, refuse an older row, and leave the table at the first sweep after the programme's end time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TMI flight list entry sets the flight's TMI update type, flight-list entry count, first FCA identifier, TMI update time and status.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The TFMS flight table has a fixed capacity: a new flight with no free slot is refused and counted, a held flight still updates, a flight silent for six hours of replay time is evicted at a sweep and its slot is reused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TFMS payload that is not well-formed XML, not a TFMS document, has a refused field or is counted under its own typed error and applies nothing; the next good payload applies. A payload with more rows than the row tables hold applies the rows that fit (OA-RPL-073).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TFMS flight row with no flight reference is not applied and is counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: FNS new, replacement and cancellation NOTAMs are keyed by series, number and year (a local-format NOTAM, which has no series, by its location in the series' place): a replacement removes the NOTAM it names and is stored, a cancellation removes the NOTAM it names and is not stored, and a replacement or cancellation naming nothing held is counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A NOTAM re-issued under a held identity replaces it whole, unless it was issued earlier than the held one, which is refused whole and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A NOTAM leaves the table at the first sweep after its end or cancelled time in replay time; one with no end time leaves after thirty days without an update; a reader can ask how many are in force at a time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A NOTAM keeps its circle, altitude limits and references, affected feature, polygon and vertex counts and the bounding box of its polygon vertices: the latitude range and the smallest longitude interval covering them, with the west end larger than the east end when the interval runs through 180 degrees.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An FNS payload that is not well-formed XML or is refused by the decoder, and a row with no usable identity, are counted under typed errors and applied to nothing; a malformed field is counted and treated as absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An ADS-B record whose position or flags are out of range is dropped and counted under the bad-record error kind, one for each; the other records of its payload are applied, and a record with only an unknown source, a bad measurement or a set reserved byte is kept.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A frame more than 2 minutes ahead of the clock and of its own feed's last frame is held, not accepted: 9.9 minutes ahead, repeated among honest frames, never moves the clock and the honest frames are never counted as regressions.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each feed's frames are compared with that feed's own last frame: feeds whose receive times differ by a constant under the tolerance count no regressions against each other, a frame before its own feed's last is still a regression, and a feed steadily more than the tolerance behind the others is held and never steps the clock.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A confirmed step marks every flight, programme and NOTAM row as stale until it is updated; the marked rows are counted (`stale_marked`) and the rows still stale can be counted at any time (`pipeline_stale_count`); eviction ages are as before.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A frame time equal to `i64::MIN`, the clock's "no frame yet" value, is held and counted, never taken as the clock or as a candidate: five such frames neither step the clock nor let a later frame a day ahead be taken as a first frame, and before the first frame it is held as well.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: (proof) `clock_observe` never panics or overflows for any clock state, feed index (any `usize`) and frame time (any `i64`, including the extremes) from any reachable candidate state (every candidate count at most `CLOCK_CONFIRM_FRAMES`); a step is returned only on the frame that completes a run of `CLOCK_CONFIRM_FRAMES` consecutive candidates of that frame's feed, with the saturated difference as its delta, every candidate count is then cleared, no step is returned from an empty candidate state, and a frame never adds candidates to another feed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: (proof) From any state the pipeline can hold (every feed with an accepted frame has it at or before the clock), one frame that is accepted moves a running clock forward by at most `CLOCK_TOLERANCE_NS` (2 minutes), or by at most `FEED_GAP_MAX_NS` (30 minutes) when no other feed has ever had an accepted frame, and the state stays consistent with the clock that results.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A feed's candidate frames behind the clock continue one run only when each is within the tolerance of the one before, in either direction: a genuine step back whose three frames arrive up to a second out of order confirms on the third; candidates ahead of the clock continue a run when each is not more than the tolerance before the one before and not more than 30 minutes after it. Candidates a day apart each start a new run and never confirm.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A confirmed step shifts every ADS-B report time by the step (when the report times follow the recorder, see OA-RPL-250) as it does the other tables' ages, and marks each aircraft stale (counted in `stale_marked`, counted by `adsb_stale_count`): a forward step of an hour keeps every aircraft that was live, and a backward step of ten minutes accepts the next genuine reports.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A confirmed step is held by the ADS-B table as pending, without moving any report time, until the next report settles whether the report times follow the recorder's clock or keep their own: the report's lag behind the clock is read both ways, and a reading fits when the report is at most 2 minutes ahead and at most 30 minutes behind. If only the first fits, or both and its lag is no larger in size, the held times shift by the step; otherwise if the second fits the table's `offset_ns` takes the step and the held times stay. A report stamped by a clock that did not step, after a forward or backward step, is applied, not refused out of order or too far ahead. Each resolution is counted (`domain_follows_clock`, `domain_kept_own`). The offset and the pending step are hashed only when either is non-zero.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Ages are measured against the clock minus the offset and the pending step, so a sweep while a step is pending evicts nobody the step did not age, however long no ADS-B frame comes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A report that fits neither reading while a step is pending is refused as too far ahead and counted, and the step stays pending until a report that fits.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Steps before the first report add; the resolution uses their sum.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The progress line's replayed span is computed with saturating arithmetic: a stream whose clock steps are each representable but whose total span is not does not stop the run.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A file is read in pieces of at most `MAX_CHUNK` bytes; its size never sets an allocation.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Offline stream advance renews its finite reader allowance only between bounded steps; over input of six scan quotas of garbage followed by a valid frame it emits that frame, conserves source bytes, takes at least five steps, and no step's measured scan, CRC, copy or compaction work exceeds one quota.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A stale mark is cleared only by an accepted update that carries what the row shows: an ADS-B report that is accepted, an SFDPS row whose position was not refused as older and that carries a position or a flight status. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A TBFM row clears the stale mark only when it carries metering state (a delete, a meter fix, a runway, a time or a freeze flag); a row of identity alone does not.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The stale marks are part of the state hash, in every table, written only when some row is stale so a replay with none hashes as it did.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A confirmed step whose size does not fit in 64 bits is not applied: the clock and every age are kept, the candidate state is kept as it was, and the step is counted under `clock-step-overflow`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The position time is written only together with a position: a row whose position is absent or malformed leaves the flight's position time as it was, whatever `positionTime` it carries, so a later valid position older than that row's time (but not older than the held one) is applied.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each flight keeps the timestamp of the newest SFDPS message applied to it. A message older than that does not change the flight's status, controlling unit or computer id and is counted as a stale amendment (`stale_amendments`). non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A claim on a flight-plan identifier held by another flight succeeds only if that flight's newest SFDPS message is older than the claiming message; otherwise the old message does not take the identifier, and is counted (`plan_refused_old`). A TBFM update for the identifier links to the owner. A claim with no source time (TBFM, or an SFDPS message with no timestamp) takes the identifier as before.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A cancelled or replaced NOTAM leaves a tombstone (identity, and the `issued` time of the cancelling or replacing notice). A new or replacing notice whose identity has a tombstone and whose `issued` time is not later than the tombstone's is refused and counted (`tomb_refused`, an out-of-order row), so a redelivery cannot bring it back; a cancellation or replacement of a NOTAM not held still leaves a tombstone, so a cancellation that arrives first holds.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tombstone is kept until the cancelled NOTAM's end (or cancelled) time if it was held and had one, else for seven days of replay time from the cancellation (a redelivery arrives within hours; a week is far past any seen), then dropped at the next sweep (`tomb_expired`). A confirmed step of the replay clock moves a tombstone held for replay time with the clock (OA-RPL-263).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tombstone's deadline records its basis: the notice's own end or cancelled time (feed time) is never moved by a clock step; the seven-day span of replay time is moved by it, forward or back, so a step never shortens a tombstone's protection (a redelivered old NEW is still refused after a forward correction past the seven days).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: When a merge or an after-frame hook ends the run with an error, the frame and gzip error counts found so far are already in the pipeline's own counts, and the error is still returned.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `replay_state_digest` covers the basis of each live NOTAM tombstone's time (a span of replay time, or the notice's own end), which decides whether a step of the replay clock moves it: two states that differ only in that flag have different digests. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A recording with a monotonic time per frame and a genuine gap (the wall time elapsed is the monotonic time elapsed, up to a difference within the clock tolerance of 2 minutes, the frame ahead of the clock) is accepted at once at its own time (`Tick::RealGap`): no age is shifted, no row is marked stale, and a flight silent for the gap expires under its age limit (an ACTIVE flight after 3 hours), also when the first frame after the gap waited seconds in the recorder before it was stamped (OA-RPL-272).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A frame whose wall time is far from the clock while the monotonic time elapsed is short (a step of +3 hours in 1 second, or a step back) is a step of the recorder's clock: handled by rules 4 to 6 as before, and counted in `Clock::mono_steps`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A recording with no monotonic time (`OAF1` frames, or `process_frame`) replays exactly as before the field existed: the same clock, tables, counters and `replay_state_digest`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `replay_state_digest` covers every time-domain decision (counts, a running hash of each decision's kind and elapsed times, and each feed's reference), written only once there is a monotonic reference or a decision, so two replays that classify a gap differently differ.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The classification at its tolerance: elapsed times differing by exactly `CLOCK_TOLERANCE_NS` (2 minutes) are time that passed, one nanosecond more is a step; a monotonic time that went back, a frame with none, and a frame behind the clock are not classified as a real gap.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Monotonic times are compared only between frames of the same stream: two recordings of the same feed from different recorder runs, whose monotonic origins happen to make a gap look genuine, are not classified, and `process_frame_mono` and `clock_observe_mono` take the stream. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The wall time elapsed since a feed's last frame is split exactly into the monotonic time elapsed (time that passed) and a step (the rest). A step within the clock tolerance is noise; a larger one goes through the candidate run, the vote and the confirmation of rules 4 to 6, and when it confirms the ages shift by the step alone (never more than the clock's move), so a gap that is partly a step ages every row by the time that passed and translates only the step. `MONO_AGREE_TOL_NS` (10 seconds) agree, one nanosecond more is a step; a monotonic time that went back, a frame with none, and a frame behind the clock are not classified as a real gap.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A cancellation removes the held NOTAM it names only when that version was issued at or before the cancellation; a version issued after it is kept and the cancellation is counted (`cancel_stale`, hashed only when not zero). Either way the cancellation leaves its tombstone, so the NOTAM held and the tombstone issued time are the same in every arrival order of a notice, its cancellation and its reissue.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The longitude cover of a wide polygon set (more than half a turn) takes the largest gap between neighbouring vertex longitudes from one sort, not a scan of every vertex against every other: the work grows as n log n, and the cover equals the pairwise method's.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tombstone table is of fixed size (set when the NOTAM table is made, by default the size of the NOTAM table); when it is full the oldest tombstone is evicted and counted (`tomb_evicted`). Tombstones are part of the state hash, after the NOTAMs, only when there are some or a tombstone counter is not zero.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Programmes whose title or element differ after byte 24 are different programmes: a longer identity is kept whole in a fixed pool of cells made at init and compared whole on lookup. A new programme whose title or element is over 512 bytes, or for which no cell is free, is refused and counted (`refused_long`, reported as a full table); two different identities are never merged.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A NOTAM is its series (or `!` and its location when it has none), number and year. A local-format row that cancels or replaces names the referred NOTAM by number and year; the referred series is `!` and the row's own location, so the cancellation removes that office's NOTAM and not another office's of the same number.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Frames reach the clock in merged receive order, so a stream whose times run ahead cannot move the clock ahead of another stream that still has frames: a stream walking 119 s per frame beside a stream talking every second for 30 minutes leaves the clock never more than the tolerance past the second stream's latest frame and never evicts its flight.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A forward run of `CLOCK_CONFIRM_FRAMES` candidates is a step with no vote (in merged order the other feeds are silent over the gap); a backward run is a step only if the feeds backing the new time (the stepping feed and every other feed with an open candidate on that side within the tolerance of the frame) are at least as many as those backing the old clock (every other feed with an accepted frame, no candidate and a last frame within the tolerance of the clock). A refused backward run is counted in `steps_outvoted` and asks again on the feed's next candidate.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A feed ten minutes behind that speaks first in merge order starts the clock; three feeds that agree ten minutes later take it with one forward step.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A step back of an hour on every feed at once is one backward step, however the frames interleave, with every age shifted (nothing evicted) and the rows marked stale.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: In a single-feed recording a gap over 30 minutes is a confirmed step (the ages carry over the pause), as for any run of three candidates.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two interleaved feeds that are both sparse (gaps over the tolerance) do not freeze the clock: the feed that speaks first runs alone while the other has no accepted frame, then the clock moves by forward steps (11 over 30 frames of each feed, 2.5 minutes apart, trailing the newest frame by under 15 minutes) with no step back.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: (proof) A step is returned only for three candidates; a backward step also needs the vote (at least as many backers of the new time as of the old clock); a refused backward step is held and counted with the run kept at the limit; three forward candidates in a row are always a step; a forward step, a backward step, a counted refusal and a lone-forward advance are each reachable.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The limit of the single-feed rule: in a single-feed recording one wild frame less than 30 minutes after the feed's last is accepted (a gap and a glitch cannot be told apart), one more than 30 minutes after it is held as a candidate.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A feed that resumes alone after a pause, with another feed's last frame just before the pause (merged order), takes a forward step after three frames: the ages of both feeds' rows are shifted and the rows marked stale, not refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The pipeline's checkpoints are held in a ring allocated at construction (`checkpoint_ring`, default 8,640, 24 hours at the default 10 s); when it is full the oldest undrained checkpoint is dropped and counted (`checkpoints_dropped` in the summary) and the ring never grows, however many checkpoints are recorded.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Consumers take checkpoints out with `pipeline_drain_checkpoints`: a run that drains as it goes (the `oa-replay` binary, the benchmark loader) drops none, even with a ring of one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `checkpoint_ring` of 0 and a checkpoint spacing under 1 second are refused when the pipeline is built (a checkpoint hashes every table, so a shorter spacing would hash on every frame).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This applies to recorded/offline replay and evaluation; the current replay path is not a live control or alert path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On two adjacent real tiles a tile set answers elevation points on both sides of the shared edge to within a metre of the owning tile, and a radius across the seam returns the highest sample of both tiles; skipped when the data is absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: GNU long names (type `L`), PAX `path` overrides and ignored keys, skipped PAX global headers, and GNU base-256 sizes are read.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Entry data the caller did not read is skipped; link, device and directory entries carry no data whatever the size field says.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A reader error is reported with the stream offset and an interrupted read is retried.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Seeded random byte damage and garbage of several lengths never panic.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: One `next_entry` call consumes at most `max_meta_records` long-name, long-link and PAX header records (zero-length ones included) and `max_meta_total_bytes` of their content; a chain longer than either is refused with a typed `TooManyMeta` error carrying the offset and the reader then refuses further calls, so a caller never waits on an unbounded run of extension headers. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This bounds a generic archive reader for offline datasets; it has no direct controller or alert effect.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An archive split into parts gives the same result as the whole; the first part alone ends in a typed truncation after delivering every complete trace before the cut; a sink error stops the scan.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is archive scanning, report/clip CLI, or offline cohort handling, not a live surveillance adapter.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is archive scanning, report/clip CLI, or offline cohort handling, not a live surveillance adapter.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--frame-ms` outside 1 to 60000, or not a whole number, is refused with exit 2 and the usage line; 1 and 60000 are accepted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is archive scanning, report/clip CLI, or offline cohort handling, not a live surveillance adapter.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is archive scanning, report/clip CLI, or offline cohort handling, not a live surveillance adapter.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The offline surface census verifies a bounded completion manifest and archive parts before counting up to 1,000,000 positioned address/time bins. It preserves explicit ground flags even when geometric elevation is present; absent altitude never implies ground. Missing, stale, mixed and non-direct-source observations remain counted and labeled. Counts are conditional on position-bearing trace observations; they imply neither total airport coverage nor runway/taxiway occupancy. Input/output provenance and partial decoding are visible, inputs remain sealed-path guarded, and every capacity refusal stops or marks the run incomplete.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is archive scanning, report/clip CLI, or offline cohort handling, not a live surveillance adapter.

Its explicit `--position-csv <private-path>` option may write every valid positioned observation in the verified bbox/time window to the fixed normalized schema, including transponder address; it must create a new distinct path, enforce the 256 MiB byte cap before each write and the 10,000,000 report-row cap, and remove/refuse incomplete output after any error. Provenance records the private CSV path, row count and hash after flush/close, plus the complete readsb `addrtype_t` source-index mapping. A partial trace decode must label the CSV partial, never complete. The optional export adds no raw positions or addresses to the counts report or stdout.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The public NCEP GEFS file (`raw/grib2-testdata/gep10.t12z.pgrb2af78.grib2`, 43 messages, 51 fields, all template 5.40) decodes with no field skipped, and its fields are physical: temperature 180 to 330 K, relative humidity 0 to 100, wind below 120 m/s, geopotential height rising as pressure falls at every point; skips when the data is absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Template 5.40 decodes a hand-built message: the codestream's samples are the packed integers and are scaled by `(R + X * 2^E) / 10^D`; a bitmap spreads the values over the grid; a field of 0 bits per value is constant and has no codestream.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Template 5.40 refuses what does not hold together: a compression type other than lossless, a sample depth or point count that differs from the section, a section that is not 23 octets, and a damaged codestream (typed `Jpeg2000(error)`); the next message of a file is still decoded.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The value count of section 5 is checked against the grid's point count (or the bitmap's set bits) before anything is unpacked or allocated, for templates 5.0, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.40, and the unpackers refuse a count beyond `MAX_GRID_POINTS` when called directly; a message claiming 4,294,967,295 values with zero bits each, or one group of that length, is refused with a typed error and nothing is sized from the claim.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A decoded value that is not finite after scaling (R, E and D can push a packed integer past the f32 range) is refused with a typed error for every packing; only a point the field marks missing comes out as NaN. `oa-wind` refuses an infinite cell when building an hour.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A complex-packed field's scratch memory (group tables, packed integers and the decoded values) is computed exactly and checked against a cap before anything is allocated: one length-one group per point with zero-bit tables and no data is refused when it exceeds the cap, and the limits are small enough to test with modelled values. The real RAP, HRRR and GEFS fields pass.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The cap is `Limits::scratch_bytes`, default 128 MiB, and does not depend on the size of the data section. A 16 Mi-point grid of length-one groups needs 448 MiB and is refused; a test builds the same construction at 300,000 points under a 1 MiB cap and sees `ScratchBudget` with the exact byte counts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Scratch is 28 bytes per point-and-group (16 per group, 12 per point): the RAP 130 grid (151,987 points) needs under 5 MB even with a group per point and HRRR CONUS (1,905,141 points) 53 MB, so an ordinary field, including a constant one, decodes under the default.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A complex field that declares more groups than points is refused with a typed error before its tables are read.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A group width is the width reference plus a 32-bit table entry, added in 64 bits and refused as `BadPacking` above 32 bits; no header field is added to or shifted before it is checked. The descriptor that overflowed 32 bits (reference 32, delta 0xFFFFFFFF) is the committed fuzz seed `fuzz/seeds/grib2/width-overflow.grib2`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A reference time (and the end of a statistical interval) must be on the Gregorian calendar: day within the month (leap years by the 4, 100, 400 rule), hour 0 to 23, minute 0 to 59, second 0 to 60; 2023-02-29, 1900-02-29, February 30 and 31 and April 31 are refused, 2000-02-29 and 2024-02-29 are read.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Product templates 4.8 and 4.11 are decoded and their interval is kept: the end of the interval, the number of time ranges and the statistical process (`Field::interval`, `None` for templates 4.0 and 4.1). The interval starts at the reference time plus the forecast time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `peek_info` reads the first field's description from the first bytes of a message (through section 5), so an inventory can be checked against a file without reading its data.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Section and message lengths that would wrap an offset are added with checked arithmetic: a damaged length at the top of the address space ends the scan or is refused with a typed error, never a panic.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies a GRIB2 decoding subset that is not connected to the accepted replay or warning path in this release.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Decoding is bounded by the input's size: one call of `decode_stream` (all its messages together) or `decode_message` may decode `work_budget(input bytes)` grid points, 4 Mi plus 64 per input byte. A field that does not fit is refused with `Grib2Error::WorkBudget` before any of it is unpacked, so a message that declares 16 Mi points in a few hundred bytes (a constant field, a flat codestream) costs nothing. The densest real input has 12.9 points per byte; reading the inventory (`inspect_stream`) is not limited.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Sector labels are read from `pdftotext -raw` text and compared with the XML: matched, mismatched, missing from the PDF and extra on the PDF are reported separately.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real FAA files (`OPENATCA_DATA/raw/mva`; the test prints the counts and skips when the data is absent) all 35 messages load with no refusal: 423 sectors, 604 rings, altitudes 2,000 to 4,300 ft, and queries at known places answer.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real files every ring closes, no polygon crosses itself, and there are no spikes, zero-area rings or holes outside their exterior.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real files no gap between the sectors of a chart is 10 raster cells (about 0.1 nm2) or larger, and no overlap is 2 nm2 or larger.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real files every sector altitude that appears on its PDF plot equals the XML value, except the two charts recorded as findings (CVG FUS3 and TOL FUS5); the test skips when `pdftotext` is absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real Rockford FUS3 chart (every chart with `OPENATCA_MVA_FULL`) the 3DEP terrain and DOF obstacle maxima are found for every sector and every margin is positive; the test skips when the terrain or DOF files are absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-mva-check` prints the load, ring, coverage, PDF and clearance sections, exits 0 when every file loads, 1 when a file is refused (naming it), and 2 on bad arguments.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This validates labels or empirical source files; it does not make the minimum-altitude decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real `raw/mva-zjx` files (skipped when absent) all 20 messages load, including `SAV_LHW_MVA` as a sub-area chart with 17 sectors.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This clause covers sample compatibility or report diagnostics, not the operational weather-to-warning calculation.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real captured files (`OPENATCA_DATA/raw/awc`; skipped with a note when absent) every file parses, every METAR, PIREP and TAF record is accepted, every hazard record is accepted or refused for `reversed-band` only (any other refusal fails the test, and each refused record is printed), a point never disagrees with its `rawSigmet` position, `altim` and `rawOb` never disagree, de-duplication counts balance, and at least 90 % of the stations in the ZAU box have a trusted altimeter in at least 95 % of the hours; the test prints the counts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This clause covers sample compatibility or report diagnostics, not the operational weather-to-warning calculation.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-awc-summary [dir]` scans a directory tree, parses each recognised file by its name, reports records, refusals by reason, duplicates, the altimeter cross-check and station availability, lists files refused whole and skipped names, and exits 1 if any file was refused whole.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This clause covers sample compatibility or report diagnostics, not the operational weather-to-warning calculation.
