non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The scan reads each file with a length check and a capped read (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`, the `oa-json` input limit); a larger file is listed as refused whole without being read.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reports are selected on NACp >= 8 (and at most 11), NIC >= 7, SIL 3 and, where the version is present, ADS-B version >= 2; a row failing one of these, carrying readsb's stale flag, or with a source other than ADS-B (MLAT, TIS-B, ADS-R, ...) is removed and counted under one named reason, and rows in always equal rows kept plus rows removed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Quality fields are carried forward within an aircraft for at most 60 s; a row with no NACp, NIC or SIL value that young is not truth and is counted as such.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A report that `oa_adsb::jump_verdict` calls impossible from the last kept one (hard cap of the emitter category, reported ground speed, time gap, plus a 200 m allowance) is removed and counted as a jump and does not affect the track; five jumps in a row start a new leg instead of rejecting the rest of the flight.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An aircraft splits into legs at readsb's new-leg flag (also when the flagged row is itself removed) and at a gap of more than 120 s between kept reports, not at exactly 120 s; leg start, end, report count and address are readable.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On a straight track with known noise (5 m per axis, 10 minutes) the smoothed position is under 4 m RMS from the true path and the velocity under 1.5 m/s RMS, the velocity points the right way, and the reported 95 % radius is above the real error and under 50 m.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On a constant-rate turn (8 km radius, 200 m/s, 5 m noise) the smoothed position is under 6 m RMS and 20 m worst, and the velocity within 5 m/s.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A leg 400 km long stays within 4 m RMS of the true path: the local frame adds no position error, and velocity is true east and north.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Barometric altitude is not smoothed: exact at a report time, the linear interpolation between the bracketing reports otherwise, absent if either lacks it; vertical rate is the reported rate interpolated, else the altitude difference over a bracket of 2 s or more.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: There is no extrapolation: no truth before a leg's first or after its last report or between legs (no bracket), none inside a leg unless a real report lies within 10 s on both sides (gap; exactly 10 s is allowed), none for an unknown address, and an address differing only in the non-ICAO bit is a different aircraft.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Truth whose 95 % horizontal radius exceeds the gate (50 m) is refused as too uncertain; the same track with precise reports, or a looser gate, is answered.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Leave-one-out hides every fifth report of each leg, predicts it from the rest under the bracket rule and publishes N, mean, RMS, median, p95, p99 and max of the horizontal, cross-track, along-track and altitude residuals, the share of predictions under the gate and the share of hidden reports inside their predicted 95 % radius; on known noise the residuals have the expected size and the radius is honest; the measurement can be switched off.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The same input gives the same truth and statistics bit for bit, in any input order, and one changed report changes the SHA-256 digest of the model.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Aircraft are keyed by the full address word, so non-ICAO addresses stay separate from ICAO ones with the same 24 bits.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Columns of different lengths and out-of-range configuration values are refused with a typed error, out-of-range coordinates are removed and counted, empty input gives an empty truth, and the gates are the design's values (NACp 8, NIC 7, SIL 3, version 2, 60 s, 120 s, 10 s, 50 m).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real ZAU ADS-B clip (skipped when `OPENATCA_ADSB_CLIP` is unset) the accounting balances, the model's 95 % radius covers 85 to 99.5 % of hidden reports, the leave-one-out horizontal p95 is under the 50 m gate, nothing is answered before an aircraft's first report, and two builds are identical.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-truth-check <clip.oaf>` reads OAF1 ADS-B frames and prints the legs, rows kept and removed by reason, the leave-one-out table, the share of query times under the uncertainty gate, the build time and the model digest (equal to the library's); `--accel-q`, `--sigma-scale` (each up to 1e6) and `--no-loo` are honoured; usage errors and unreadable input exit 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An aircraft flying 900 kt in a straight line and reporting 900 kt gives one continuous leg with no report removed as a jump, at 1 s and at 3 s between reports.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A position jump of 2,782 kt in a 450 kt track is removed and counted, whether or not the reports carry a ground speed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reports of the reserved addresses 0x000000 and 0xFFFFFF are removed as invalid and give no aircraft or leg; the same digits with the non-ICAO mark are kept.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The quality values carried forward within an aircraft come only from rows that are in range, not stale and from an ADS-B source: a row from another source does not vouch for the ADS-B rows after it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Rows of one aircraft at one instant do not make the truth depend on input order. Two eligible reports (see OA-TRUTH-024) conflict when their squared horizontal distance exceeds 13.82 (the 2-degree-of-freedom chi-square value at 99.9 %) times the sum of their squared per-axis sigmas, each the NACp 95 % radius over 2.4477; errors are assumed independent. A conflicting group is removed whole (counted as duplicate times); the rest are tried in the order of their content, so the same reports in any input order give the same truth and statistics. The 50 m limit gates the reference's output uncertainty only (OA-TRUTH-010), not this pair rule.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The emitter category that sets the jump cap is taken only from reports that pass the quality rules and are kept, and a cap-raising one must persist (`oa_adsb::category_observe`): one report printing B7 or a reserved code does not let a 2,782 kt jump into truth, and a category printed by every report does raise the cap after three.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-truth-check` on a clip that ends inside a frame (a partial header or a partial body) keeps the valid frames and counts the partial frame in the frames it prints as refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Whether a same-time row takes part in the conflict check is decided by the full selection (coordinates, NACp, NIC, SIL, version, stale flag, source) against the carried quality as it was before the instant; an ineligible row is removed for its own reason and cannot veto a usable one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The result for same-time rows does not depend on their order in the input, including when one of them is ineligible.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Same-time rows identical in position and NACp are collapsed before the conflict check, so 1,000 identical rows cost no pair evaluations beyond the rows themselves.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: More than 16 distinct eligible same-time rows of one aircraft are refused and counted under `oversized_same_time_group`; 16 are tested pairwise.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two NACp 8 reports 70 m apart at one instant (each inside its 92.6 m 95 % radius) are kept as one position measured twice.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two same-time reports far beyond the bound of OA-TRUTH-022 are quarantined.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A mixed-NACp same-time pair is judged at its own bound: NACp 8 with NACp 10 is kept at 139 m and quarantined at 144 m (bound 141.5 m).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A row removed as a jump does not change the carried quality: a following report that prints none gets the same selection and weight with or without the jump row.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A low-quality row that is also a jump does not remove later usable reports; a low-quality row on the track still does.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A `sigma_scale` or `accel_q` above 1e6 is refused at configuration (`BadConfig`): the covariance squares them and would overflow to infinity and NaN.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A variance that is NaN or infinite has no horizontal radius: the query refuses it as too uncertain, the uncertainty statistics count it as a miss, and a leave-one-out prediction with a non-finite state or variance counts as not predicted. It is never zero uncertainty.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A query whose converted latitude, longitude or velocity is not finite (a state past the frame's chart) is refused as too uncertain, never returned as a sample.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A `--accel-q` or `--sigma-scale` value of `oa-truth-check` that is not a finite number above zero is a usage error, before the clip is read.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A difference of two report times that does not fit an `i64` never panics: the builder splits the leg there, queries refuse it as no nearby report, and interpolation and the leave-one-out bracket treat it as no interval.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A time difference is never saturated: where it can exceed an `i64` (the quality carry age, the query bracket, interpolation) the overflow reads as "not within", and the steps of one leg the smoother subtracts without a check never exceed `leg_gap_ms`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-truth-check` refuses a clip over 4 GiB before reading it, and a clip whose frame headers claim more than 50 million rows before decoding the frame that crosses the cap (typed `ClipError`). Ten times the largest real day (330 MB, 4.07 million rows). `oa-sensorsim` reads clips through the same reader (`oa_truth::clip::read_clip`), so it has the same caps.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Proved (Kani, `clip_row_count_refuses_exactly_when_the_total_crosses_the_cap`, `clip_claim_rows_is_total`): the row count the clip reader accumulates from frame headers cannot wrap, and it refuses at the first frame whose exact running total is over the cap, and at no other.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Of several accepted rows of one aircraft at one instant the builder keeps the one that carries the most fields, in the preference order barometric altitude, geometric altitude, vertical rate, ground speed, track (`preference` in `build.rs`; a row with a valid value earlier in the list wins), then by content. A row whose altitude is absent never wins over one whose altitude is valid, whatever the input order.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Eligible rows of one instant with two valid barometric (or two valid geometric) altitudes more than `ALT_QUANTUM_FT` (25 ft) apart make the instant ambiguous: all its eligible rows are dropped, counted as `ambiguous_same_time_altitude`, and the instant is not truth; the pick is never arbitrary and does not depend on input order. Rows whose positions differ beyond their stated NACp are dropped and counted as `duplicate_time`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A state past the chart of the leg's frame (the antipode of its origin) is refused as too uncertain; no NaN velocity or position is returned as truth. The velocity conversion uses `oa_geo::aeqd::try_frame_velocity` and handles `None`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every limit of `TruthConfig` is exact: NACp gate 1 to 11, NIC at most 11, SIL at most 3, version at most 7, carry time not negative and the other time gates positive and at most one day, floating settings finite and positive (the covariance ones capped), jump allowance zero or more, `jump_resync` at least 1, `min_leg_points` at least 3, `loo_stride` at least 2; each is accepted at the limit and refused one step beyond. `MAX_REPORTS` is 200 Mi reports, exactly that many are accepted and one more refused, and every `TruthError` has its message text.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Rows of one instant: the kept row is the first in the order barometric altitude, geometric altitude, vertical rate, ground speed, track, whichever input order; geometric as well as barometric altitudes more than 25 ft apart make the instant ambiguous (25 ft is not), an absent one does not; every pair of distinct eligible positions is compared once and no pair twice.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A report that fails on quality still sets the quality values the reports after it carry (a NACp of 7 is not forgotten, so the following reports without a NACp fail with it); one of several rows of an instant that fails does not.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A leg whose reports pass 3,000 km (0.4709 rad of arc) from its first report is split there and counted under `frame_range`, at the first report past the limit and not before.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The measurement sigma of a report is its NACp 95 % radius over 2.4477 times `sigma_scale` (checked on the forward covariance of the first report against the Kalman update); the shares of report times and interval midpoints under the gate count intervals up to and including twice the bracket (20 s), compare the radius at the midpoint (not at the earlier report), and are exact against the Kalman/RTS covariance.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Queries: a radius exactly at the gate is truth, a velocity well past the speed envelope is not; the vertical rate is the interpolated reported rates when both are present, else the altitude difference over a bracket of at least 2 s, else absent; a leg's first whole millisecond rounds up and its last rounds down (before 1970 too); a leg with no reports has no start, end or count.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each quality gate passes at its limit and fails one step below (NACp 8 to 11, NIC 7, SIL 3, version 2); a row missing any one of NACp, NIC or SIL has no quality, a missing version is allowed; the NACp and NACv tables are the standard's values.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Leave-one-out: positions 2, 7, 12 and so on of a leg are hidden; a leg with fewer than three reports left, a hidden report with no remaining report on a side, one more than 10 s away on either side, or a prediction with a non-finite state or variance is counted as not predicted and adds no residual; horizontal, along-track and cross-track residuals, the coverage test (residual against 2.4477 times the root of the predicted plus the report variance), the gate share and the altitude residual (time-weighted neighbours, all three present) equal values worked out from the filter equations; distributions are the signed mean, the RMS and the nearest-rank median, p95, p99 and maximum.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The smoother's forward and smoothed states and full covariances, and the interpolated state and covariance between and at reports, equal the Kalman and Rauch-Tung-Striebel equations evaluated independently; the process noise is the white-jerk matrix element by element; the 3 x 3 inverse is exact and a singular or non-finite matrix has none.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-truth-check` prints each removal reason with its count, the removal total beside the kept and input counts, the shares as `percent (hit of n)` (`n/a` with no sample), the records dropped from decoded frames when there are any and only then, and refuses an unknown option, a missing value and a second path with the usage text.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The clip reader's caps are 4 GiB and 50 million rows; a row total exactly at the cap is accepted and one past it refused; after the cap is crossed later frames change nothing; frames that are not messages are ignored; dropped records, undecodable payloads and a cut frame are each counted once; `ClipError` has its message texts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The truth digest hashes a float's IEEE bits through `oa_math::canon_nan`: two truths that differ only in the sign or payload of a NaN in any float column or setting have the same digest, and a truth that differs in a finite value does not.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every statistic reports N, the signed mean, the RMS, and the median, 95th and 99th percentile and maximum of the absolute values, by the nearest-rank method (rank `ceil(p*n/100)`, 1-based, no interpolation); the result does not depend on the order of the values, non-finite values are skipped, and an empty set gives N = 0.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every paired-sample metric is split by flight phase (climb, cruise, descent, unknown from the truth vertical rate, 500 fpm), altitude band (breaks at 10,000, 18,000, 29,000 and 41,000 ft), coast flag and association method; each split partitions the samples.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Truth is consumed as `Truth { query(addr, t_ms) -> Result<TruthSample, NoTruth>, legs }` with `TruthSample` (lat, lon, baro altitude, east and north velocity, vertical rate, 95% horizontal uncertainty, leg) and `NoTruth` (unknown aircraft, no bracket, too uncertain, gap); a time with no truth is counted in the exclusions table by reason and never filled in, and a sample whose uncertainty exceeds the gate (50 m) is excluded as too uncertain.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: SFDPS extraction reads ERAM track samples (flight key, aircraft identification, position time, receive time, position, reported altitude, track velocity, coast flag), the aircraft address and the address hint, handoff events with their event kind and both units, and expanded-route points (fix, time, coordinates where given) into struct-of-arrays tables, using the `oa-fixm` decoder.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TBFM extraction keeps ETA at the meter fix and runway and STA at the scheduling fix and runway with the meter fix, flight plan identifier and issue time; TFMS extraction keeps estimated arrival and departure times with the flight plan identifier, airports and issue time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every table has a stated capacity; a row past it is dropped and counted by table, and a document the parser or decoder refuses is counted by feed and not ingested.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Association takes `aircraftAddress` first, the address hint second and the callsign with the gate last; ambiguous flights (two aircraft pass the gate) are not associated and are counted; every flight has one outcome, the outcomes are counted, and the samples of unassociated flights are excluded by reason.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The callsign check compares the ERAM position with the truth: a flight with at least 80% of the shared times within 3 NM horizontally and 1,000 ft vertically is associated as method callsign; one that fails the check is still associated, under its own method, so it never leaves the results; the address needs no such check; the method is stored per pair and every metric can be split by it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Cross-track error (T1, positive to the right of the truth track) recovers an injected bias and noise; along-track error (T2) is reported raw and after fitting one constant time offset by least squares (`along = tau * speed`), the offset is published, and the corrected error recovers the injected noise.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The fitted offset drifts when a time bin (or, after trimming 5% either side, an aircraft group) of at least 30 samples differs from the overall offset by more than 1 s; a drifting offset withholds the corrected along-track numbers with the reason while the offset and the raw numbers stay published; a large steady offset is not drift.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Speed error (T3), heading error (T3, truth speed above 30 kt) and altitude error (T4) recover injected biases.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Publication interval (T5, consecutive position times of one flight, repeats and intervals over 600 s counted apart) and staleness (T6, receive time minus position time, withheld with the reason when the recording has no receive time) are measured from the stream.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Presence (T7: share of truth flight time in the zone with an ERAM position within 30 s, legs with no associated flight counting as absent) and initiation delay (T8: first ERAM position minus zone entry or takeoff, signed) match the construction.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Association errors (T9: the ERAM position closer to another aircraft's truth than to its own for 3 or more consecutive tested samples) find the deliberate track swap, list it with both aircraft, and report none where there is none.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Meter-fix ETA error (F1) and scheduled-time error (F2) against the truth crossing of the fix (closest approach within 2 NM, not at the end of a truth leg) are reported by look-ahead in 5-minute bins to 60 minutes; a fix never approached and an estimate issued after the crossing are excluded and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TFMS arrival-estimate error against the truth landing (last truth point on the ground within 1 NM of a destination threshold) and departure-estimate error against the truth takeoff are reported by look-ahead. On the ground is judged in feet above mean sea level (OA-BENCH-110).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Route conformance (R1) reports the truth distance from ERAM's expanded route in force at each sample, the share of flight time beyond 2 NM, and lists each flight with time beyond it (bounded, the rest counted).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Handoff timing (H1) compares the initiation and acceptance event times with the truth crossing of the boundary between the transferring and receiving unit, signed, by event. A crossing time is taken only where the truth is continuous across it (OA-BENCH-100).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Samples and estimates that cannot be scored are counted in an exclusions table keyed by scope and reason (no truth by kind, not associated by outcome, no meter fix, never within 2 NM, no route, and others); nothing is dropped silently.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report carries the input file hashes, the code version, the replay state hash, the extraction counts, the scope statement (published track, not internal), the statistics definitions, every metric with N and its withheld reason if any, and the exclusions table, in plain text and CSV.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The same inputs give byte-identical text and CSV reports.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A directory of raw `.msg` files (name order, no receive time, no replay hash) or of `.oaf` recordings (receive times, replay pipeline state hash, identical on repeat) loads; the input hash of one file is its SHA-256 and of several is the SHA-256 of the `name:sha256` lines.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The `oa-bench` binary refuses `--adsb` without `--out` and a non-positive truth gate override (exit 2), runs the synthetic world with `--synthetic --out <dir>` writing `report.txt` and `report.csv` with every self-test check passing and identical bytes on a repeat, and prints extraction counts with `--extract-only`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real 2026-11-14 sample (skipped when absent) extraction yields the expected counts: 13,268 ERAM track samples, 2,807 handoff events, 265 expanded routes with 1,397 points, 165 flights with `aircraftAddress`, no capacity drops, and no refused TBFM or TFMS document.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The synthetic self-test (closed-form truth; injected bias, noise, time offset, decimation, receive delay, coasting, dropout, start delay, estimate errors, handoff times, an off-route stretch and a track swap) is recovered by every metric within its stated tolerance (26 checks, the last two on the callsign-only aircraft with a 20 km error that stays in the headline).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A truth built from a plain lookup table and the same legs gives the same paired samples and metrics as the closed-form truth, so the interface needs nothing but the query and the legs.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The address hint associates a flight that has no aircraftAddress, is stored as its own method, and a hint with no truth aircraft is not retried by callsign.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-truth` query answers map onto the benchmark's truth interface reason for reason: unknown aircraft, outside legs, no nearby report and too uncertain each map to the same-named benchmark reason with the same meaning; a sample keeps its position, velocity, uncertainty and leg, with altitude and vertical rate rounded to whole units.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Truth legs are `oa-truth`'s legs in index order with their first and last whole millisecond; the leg callsign is the most frequent callsign among the decoded reports of the address inside the leg's span, and `None` when no report carries one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The truth gates come from `oa-truth`'s configuration (design: 10 s bracket, 50 m); the bracket and uncertainty overrides change it, and the report's truth section carries the gates, the statistics, the removals by reason, the leave-one-out table and the truth digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An OAF1 ADS-B clip is read through `oa-feed` and `oa-adsb` into reports, counting frames that did not decode, and its SHA-256 is the input hash.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The airspace lookups come from the M0 model: fixes and navaids by identifier (not airports), airports by ICAO and FAA identifier with elevation and thresholds, the model's ARTCC as the zone, and the containing ARTCC as the unit where exactly one contains the point (OA-BENCH-111).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-bench --adsb <clip.oaf>` runs end to end: on a hand-made clip and SFDPS fixture whose track is 500 m left of the truth, T1 recovers -500 m (cross-track, positive right) within 2 m with every sample paired; the report holds the truth section, the clip hash and the gate values, a repeat gives identical bytes, and an override of the gates is recorded in the header with its reason.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: On the real ADS-B clip and the SCDS sample (skipped when `OPENATCA_DATA` or `OPENATCA_ADSB_CLIP` is unset), whose times do not overlap, the run completes with no paired samples and an exclusions table.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Association never depends on the error being measured. A callsign flight is kept when truth overlaps it in time (at least 5 shared times) and lies within 50 NM of its positions for 80% of them; a flight that fails the 3 NM / 1,000 ft check is associated all the same under its own method (callsign, failed the check), counted in the headline rows, split out by the method split, and listed as a case. Two or more callsign candidates are ambiguous.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An address or address-hint association is checked without using ERAM's accuracy: callsigns that contradict (both known, none of the truth legs agrees) or ERAM positions beyond the 50 NM region for more than 20% of the shared times make it implausible; with too few shared times it is trusted and counted as unchecked. An implausible flight is not in the primary rows and its cross-track, raw along-track and altitude errors are published in separate flagged tables, each flight listed with its reason; an address with a believable error is trusted as before.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The statistics of an empty set have n = 0 and NaN in every other field, never 0.0; the text report prints such a row as "no data" and the CSV as `NA`; scalars of an empty set (presence, share of time beyond the route limit, largest per-flight share, offset deviations with nothing tested) are NaN and print the same way; no report contains the text `NaN`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Raw along-track error is the primary along-track result and the offset-corrected one is secondary, and says that the fitted offset cannot be told apart from real ERAM lag. The offset is published with its sample standard error, its between-aircraft standard error and a 95% half-width (1.96 times the larger); the drift test keeps its 5% trim and also publishes the untrimmed largest group deviation and the five worst aircraft groups.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tracker's output columns are scored by the same code path as ERAM's samples: the tracker entry point is the legacy-table adapter followed by the one benchmark function, gives a report identical to calling the two directly, and yields the same metrics, in the same order, with the same offset scalars and notes as an ERAM run; a tracker that lags the truth shows the lag in the raw along-track error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tracker's output scored in address ranges gives the report of the same rows scored in one piece, byte for byte in the text and the CSV, whatever order the flights are in the table and whatever order the ranges are added in: the case lists (association, T9) are sorted by severity, truth address and time before they are cut to 200, and every sum behind a statistic (means, RMS, the along-track offset fit) is exactly rounded, so the order of the values cannot change a bit. T5 is summed from whole milliseconds in both paths.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Scoring in address ranges refuses ranges that overlap, ranges that together leave any key from 0 to 0xFFFFFFFF uncovered (the radar-only tracks keyed from 0x40000000 included), and a chunk with a flight keyed or associated outside its range; no flight or truth leg is counted twice or dropped.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The headline tables T1, T2-raw and T4 carry the number of flagged flights and of their paired samples that they leave out (`flagged_flights_excluded`, `flagged_points_excluded`) and a last row, "all associated including flagged", over the headline and the flagged samples together; the other rows are unchanged, and the run in ranges gives the same.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A chunk scored in address ranges is accepted only when its plan-data results (F1 to F3, R1, H1) equal exactly what a table with no data gives, NaN included; a result that differs only in a NaN is refused, not read as empty.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The association of a run in address ranges is the real one, one entry per flight with the chunks' associations in range order, and its counts equal those of the run in one piece; it is never an empty stand-in.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reading an ADS-B clip drops only a record that cannot be read (position or flags out of range), counts it apart from refused frames, and keeps the other records of its frame.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A route is never joined across a point that cannot be placed: an expanded route with an unplaced point between two others is excluded and counted (a dogleg whose middle fix is unknown is not scored as the straight line, whatever the truth does), while unplaced points at either end only shorten it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A fix identifier that names more than one place is never resolved by row order: the airspace lookup lists every distinct place (rows at one place are one place), answers a single place only when there is one, and counts the ambiguous identifiers; a route chooses the place clearly nearest to the previous placed point and otherwise is excluded and counted; a meter fix is the one place inside the zone or the estimate is excluded and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Meter-fix crossings, takeoffs and landings are taken from the one truth leg that overlaps the flight plan's active interval the most (the 60 minutes after issue when the plan has no ERAM sample) and cached per leg (a meter fix per passage, OA-BENCH-071): one aircraft flying two trips with a perfect estimate for each scores zero error on both.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A truth leg that begins or ends near a runway threshold with no barometric altitude is not a takeoff or landing: the estimate is excluded and counted with that reason.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The common-time comparison scores two systems at the same truth times: two systems with the same error at every instant but different publication rates have different native RMS and equal common-time RMS, a grid time counts only when both have a paired sample within the tolerance, and the grid times left out are counted (duplicate tracks: OA-BENCH-070).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The legacy extraction accepts exactly the documents the replay pipeline accepts: both build their parser and decoders from the replay's one definition of the limits (`doc_xml_limits`, `doc_fixm_limits`, the table sizes) and both decode as far as the tables fit, so a 2 MiB SFDPS document with ignored text, and SFDPS, TBFM and TFMS documents with more rows than a table holds, give the same accepted row counts in both, not a whole refused document in one and a kept prefix in the other. The rows past the table are counted (`rows_not_decoded`) and the report shows the documents the extraction refused over all feeds.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight plan identifier that more than one flight used never joins an estimate to the first flight: the plan index keeps every flight of an identifier (bounded; flights past the bound are counted), and an estimate resolves to the one flight whose active interval (the interval of OA-BENCH-052) contains its issue time and whose callsign does not contradict the aircraft identification the estimate carries. No such flight, or more than one, excludes the estimate with a named reason. The result does not depend on the order the flights were ingested in.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An ADS-B clip that ends inside a frame (a partial header or a partial body) keeps its valid frames and counts the partial frame with the frames it refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The digest of an input file is computed from the bytes that are ingested, in the same read: a file that changes between listing and reading, or while it is read, gives the digest of the bytes scored, never of another copy. `.msg` files are hashed as they are read, `.oaf` and `.oaf.gz` recordings as the replay merge reads them and the ADS-B clip as its frame loop reads it; a file whose read does not reach its end is an error, not a digest. The report notes this for the feed inputs and for the clip. A `.msg` file past the size limit is refused (OA-BENCH-092).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An estimate whose plan identifier names one recorded flight joins it unless both carry an aircraft identification and the two differ (the identifier was reused by a flight outside the recording): then it is excluded with a named reason. There is no time check for a lone flight, so an estimate issued before the flight's first ERAM sample still joins.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An estimate whose plan identifier was used by more flights than the plan index keeps is excluded with a named reason, never resolved against the flights kept; the overflow count is in the report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Among several flights of one plan identifier, an estimate goes to the one flight whose callsign equals its aircraft identification (OA-BENCH-090) when exactly one does, even if its issue time is outside that flight's active interval (an estimate issued before the flight's first ERAM sample is not handed to the neighbouring flight or dropped); otherwise the active interval of OA-BENCH-052, with its 60-minute rule for a flight with no ERAM sample, decides.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The digest covers every byte of every read, including reads after a zero-length read; the digest of a file whose last read was not a zero-length read is an error, not a digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The common-time comparison never picks a row by its error: among rows of one system for one aircraft at one time (several flight records), it uses the row of the flight with the most paired samples for that aircraft over the whole run, the lowest flight index on a tie, whatever the grid phase; every other row at that time is counted as a duplicate-track sample and reported beside C1 for each system.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each contiguous stretch of a truth leg inside the 2 NM radius of a meter fix is one passage, its time the closest approach within the stretch. An estimate is scored against the first passage that ends after its issue time (the passage it is issued in, when issued inside one); the estimated time never chooses it. A leg crossing a fix at 11:30 and again at 12:30 scores an estimate issued at 12:05 against 12:30. Passages are cached per (leg, fix, passage). F3 takes one takeoff (leg start) and one landing (leg end) per leg, so it has no second occurrence in a leg to choose between.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report header carries metrics version 2 and a scoring-code digest: SHA-256, in hex, over the name, length and text of the metric modules (included at build, hashed at run time), plus the build's `OPENATCA_SOURCE_REV` when set. A change to those modules changes the digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every join on an identifier compares one normal form: leading white space skipped, cut at the first zero or white space, ASCII upper case, zero padded. That covers callsign against aircraft identification (one flight or several), plan identifier in the plan index and in every lookup into it (TBFM, TFMS, the matching counts), and fix and airport names against the airspace model. Two accepted spellings of one identifier (case, padding) never score differently.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The extraction counts list what the decoders refused: SFDPS messages rejected by reason and field errors in kept rows by field, TBFM flights and TFMS messages refused for a field by field index and by reason, each with its total. The arrival assigned-altitude rescan also breaks unsupported FIXM roots down into absent roots, other local names and `MessageCollection` roots with a non-NAS namespace, without reporting raw names or namespace values. A row or field that did not reach scoring is in one of the counts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An input file is bounded. A `.msg` file longer than the replay parser's document limit plus 64 KiB, by its length or because it grows while read, is not kept: it is read to its end through a fixed buffer and refused as a document (OA-BENCH-102). The airspace snapshot is read with a cap against the snapshot size limit and refused (the load fails, naming the file) when longer. No read allocates more than the limit.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A handoff crossing time is derived from truth only where the truth is continuous across the boundary: the last sample over the transferring unit and the first over the receiving unit are no further apart than the truth leg gap (`oa_truth::LEG_GAP_MS`) and the unit is known at every refinement probe. Otherwise the handoff is excluded as "crossing inside a truth gap" and counted. With several crossings in the window the one nearest the event is used.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Mean and RMS are summed on values scaled by a power of two near the largest magnitude, so finite input gives no overflow or underflow to a perfect value: `[1e200]` has RMS 1e200, values near `f64::MAX` and the smallest subnormal give their RMS, and one huge value among ordinary ones is not lost. A statistic still not finite is NaN (not computable), never 0.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A `.msg` file longer than a document can be is counted as a refused document of its feed with the reason "longer than a document can be" and the load continues; its bytes are all in the input digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A fix passage whose stretch inside the radius begins or ends at a hole in the truth has no closest-approach time. The sum of squared milliseconds behind a histogram RMS that leaves the range of a `u128` gives an RMS of NaN, not a wrapped or panicking one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The takeoff and landing ground test never compares pressure altitude with field elevation (feet above mean sea level). The truth altitude becomes `pressure_alt + (altimeter inHg - 29.92) * 1000` with the field's METAR altimeter setting nearest in time and within 60 minutes (the earlier of two equally near; a value outside 27 to 32 inHg is no setting). A field with no such setting excludes the event as "no altimeter setting for the field" and counts it; nothing is assumed (`oa-bench --metar <dir>` supplies the settings, and without it every such event is excluded).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A point inside the areas of more than one ARTCC has no unit: facility-name order never chooses. A handoff whose truth window holds such a point is excluded from H1 as "truth position inside more than one ARTCC area, unit ambiguous" and counted, and the report lists each overlapping facility pair with the number of such positions examined.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Distances and east-north error components use the WGS-84 geodesic inverse and direct solutions of `oa-geo`, not a small-distance tangent plane: 89.99 N at 0 E and 180 E are 2233.9 m apart with the other point due north, 90 degrees along the equator is 10 018 754 m, and a mid-latitude pair agrees with the old tangent plane to a tenth of a percent. An invalid position gives NaN, which the pairing excludes and counts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `dist_to_polyline` is the exact WGS-84 geodesic distance to the nearest geodesic segment (`oa_airspace::geom::exact_edge_m`), within 1 m of a dense-sampling brute force on a 600 NM segment.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The synthetic world's truth velocity (and the velocity of its ERAM stream) is true east and north at the aircraft's position, the plane velocity carried through the same geodesic map as the positions: its heading equals the heading of the position track to 0.01 degrees.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The bench publishes `T3-heading-grid`: the heading error regressed on `(lon - mean lon) * sin(lat)`, with slope, standard error, count and the reference longitude; slope 1 for an injected error equal to that term, 0 for none.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A handoff crossing time is given only where the truth is available and definite at every probe of the search and on both sides of the bracket; a crossing that may lie inside a gap in the truth is excluded and counted as "crossing inside a truth gap". Without a gap it is located to 1 s.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: T8 is the time of the first associated position of the leg minus the zone entry, or, for a leg that starts inside the zone, minus its observed takeoff (OA-BENCH-125). A value of zero or less is not a delay: it is counted as `established_before_entry` and left out of the distribution; a pop-up 20 s after entry gives 20 s.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `legacy_from_track_samples_by_leg` makes one flight per truth leg of an address (a row goes to the latest leg of its address starting at or before its time), so the publication interval (T5) is never taken between two trips of one aircraft.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `check_split` refuses a split of the ADS-B reports into the tracker's set A and the truth's set B when an (address, time) is in both sets or a set holds two reports of the same address, time and content: a typed violation, a hard error of the run and not a warning.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `score_track_samples` and the `oa-track` scorer build the legacy table by truth leg, so T5 of a scored run is per trip, not pooled across the trips of one address.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `observation_key` is the one identity of an ADS-B report for the split and its check: address, time and every field scoring or quality handling reads (position, altitudes, vertical rate, speed, track, squawk, flags, source, category, NIC, NACp, NACv, SIL, SIL type, version). Reports of one address and time that differ in any of them are not copies: they stay together on one side, ordered by the key, so the retained evidence and the scores do not depend on input order.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `load_metar_dir` reads each METAR file once into memory and hashes and parses those bytes, so the reported digest describes the data scored even if the file changes between reads.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `T3-heading-grid` does not depend on the order of the pairs: longitudes are taken relative to the smallest longitude of the samples and the samples are summed in sorted order. A cohort spanning more than 90 degrees of longitude is refused (scalar `refused_span` is 1, no slope), not fitted to an arbitrary anchor.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `stats_of` keeps in the mean what scaling by a power of two rounds away from values too small for the scaled range: `[1e308, -1e308, 1e-300]` has mean 3.33e-301, equal to the exact sum over the count.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A takeoff in T8 is an observed event: the first airborne ADS-B report after a ground report inside the truth leg (`LegStart::Takeoff`, with the gap back to the last ground report as the stated uncertainty, `takeoff_time_uncertainty_s_max`). A leg that begins inside the zone is measured from its takeoff; one whose first stated ground state is airborne is excluded and counted as `legs_first_seen_airborne_in_zone`, one never airborne as `legs_starting_inside_zone_never_airborne`, one with no ground indication as `legs_starting_inside_zone_no_ground_report`. No altitude cutoff is used.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: T7 counts every grid point whose truth query failed, by reason (`truth_grid_points_failed_*`), with the total and the usable points, and says that presence is conditional on usable truth; a leg with no usable truth at any point is counted as `legs_no_usable_truth`, not as never in the zone.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A pair whose truth ground speed is below 30 kt is left out of the heading statistics with a counted reason, `T3-heading: truth speed below 30 kt`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The airspace lookups keep airports of two ICAO regions that share an identifier apart: thresholds join the airport of their own region, and an identifier naming airports of more than one region is not answered and is counted (`ambiguous_airports`).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Rows, samples and values the benchmark leaves out are counted under a named reason and reported, not dropped: tracker rows of a flight the table refuses, SFDPS, TBFM and TFMS rows ingest cannot place, samples left out of the T2 offset fit and of the common-time comparison (non-finite or slow), and truth states with a non-finite or out-of-range altitude or vertical rate, which are refused as `NoTruth::NotFinite`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: T9 names the nearest other aircraft the same way whatever the order of the legs: of two at the same distance, the lower address, with such samples counted (`nearest_tied_samples`). The legs looked at over a call are bounded by `SwapConfig::max_leg_visits`; a sample past it is refused and counted (`samples_refused_work_budget`). T9 measures nearness, not identity.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: T4 compares ERAM altitude with the truth on ERAM's own reference. A reported value at or above 18,000 ft is a flight level, compared with the truth pressure altitude as it is. A lower value is an altitude set with the local altimeter setting, so the truth is first brought to indicated altitude with `pressure altitude + (inHg - 29.92) * 1000` ft, using the setting of the nearest station (by position) that has one within 60 minutes of the sample (the setting nearest in time). A pair with no setting is not compared: it is counted under `T4` / `no altimeter setting`, never compared uncorrected. T4 reports `compared_as_flight_level`, `corrected_with_altimeter`, `excluded_no_altimeter_setting` and `mean_altimeter_correction_ft`; the flagged view applies the same correction.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
