non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Where a flight's `aircraftAddress` fails the plausibility check or is unknown to truth, and its `ADSB_02M_*` address hint is a different address, known to truth, that passes the check (not merely unchecked), the flight is associated with the hint under its own status and method (`hint over plan`); its pairs are scored in the primary rows as that method split, and each such flight is listed with both addresses and the reason the plan address failed. A plausible plan address always wins; an unchecked hint never replaces it, and a plan address that is only unchecked (too few shared times) is kept. `AssocConfig::hint_over_plan` (default on) turns the rule off for protocols frozen before it. The case list holds the first 200 cases by severity; the ASSOC table counts the cases left out ("more cases not listed") and the truth addresses associated with more than one ERAM flight at the same time (time spans, first to last sample, that overlap; consecutive legs do not), and lists them.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The flight table keeps the last transponder code an SFDPS message gave (`currentBeaconCode`, four octal digits read as a decimal number like the ADS-B squawk) in `Flights::beacon`, and `NO_BEACON` when no message carried one; a message without a valid code leaves the stored one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `Legacy::beacons` holds one row (flight, message time, code) each time a message gives a flight a code other than the one it had, the first code included, so the code in force at a time is the last row of the flight at or before it. The table is capped (`Limits::beacons`); a row that does not fit, or whose message has no time, is counted under the notes and not stored.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A beacon change beyond the cap is counted under the label `DROP_SFDPS_BEACON_FULL` and the flight still holds the last code.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `Legacy::tfms_actual` holds the TFMS arrival times of type ACTUAL, apart from `Legacy::tfms`; a row that does not fit is counted in `overflow_tfms_actual`, and neither the table nor the counter appears in any oa-bench report line.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Pressure altitude becomes pressure by the ICAO standard atmosphere (exact, since pressure altitude is defined on the ISA): 1013.25 hPa at 0 ft, 506.0 at FL180, 300.9 at FL300, 226.32 at the tropopause, continuous across it, and the inverse round-trips. Non-finite input and altitudes outside -5000 m to 20 000 m are refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Horizontal interpolation is bilinear in the grid's own coordinates; a field linear in the grid indexes is reproduced exactly at any position inside the grid.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Vertical interpolation is linear in log-pressure between the bracketing isobaric levels; a field linear in ln p is reproduced exactly between levels, and the aircraft's pressure altitude is converted through the ISA pressure.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: U and V stored grid-relative (the grid's component flag) are rotated to east and north by the convergence angle at the query longitude; a uniform earth-relative wind stored grid-relative is recovered, is wrong without the rotation, and a grid that is already earth-relative is not rotated.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Time is linear between the two bracketing analysis hours; the answer reports the hours used and the weight; on an hour the weight is 0 (or 1 against the previous hour for the last).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A query is refused with a typed `Refusal` outside the grid, above or below the level range (the limits themselves are answered), outside the time span by even one second, outside the ISA range, for non-finite input, and with no hours; never extrapolated.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A missing value at a grid corner or level that the query uses is refused as `MissingValue`, never filled; a query that does not touch it is answered (OA-WIND-052).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An hour is built only from complete, consistent fields: a level lacking U, V, T or height, a repeated field, differing grids, point counts or valid times, a fractional level, an unusable time unit, fewer than two levels and more than 64 levels are refused with typed errors; other parameters and non-isobaric levels are ignored; the arrays are level-major in ascending pressure.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Bytes that are not a GRIB2 file with the needed fields are refused, and an hour is loaded by decoding only the isobaric UGRD, VGRD, TMP and HGT messages (the rest are only inspected).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The `.idx` byte ranges of exactly the isobaric UGRD, VGRD, TMP and HGT messages are selected (layer labels such as `500-1000 mb` and other variables excluded) and adjacent ranges joined.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines generated truth, reference alignment, or study scoring; those values are evaluation inputs, never operational identity or track inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The archive refuses two files with one valid time and too many files, sorts by time, refuses queries before reading any file where it can, reports an unreadable file as a typed error, and holds at most three hours.

Generic XML tests establish only well-formed XML parsing and explicit security refusals; ASDI XML payload/XSD semantics and TFMDI file profiles are not implemented, and the SWIM TFMData decoder is not treated as a TFMDI decoder. Historical pins were recorded again at OA-TRK-077 and OA-TRK-078, which changed five duplicate counts; changes to prediction equations require a fresh comparison with that full-state reference.

The full default table and rollback pool fit within 2,300 bytes per track plus the raw-altitude history from OA-TRK-355 (32 bytes per track and 32 bytes per reserved snapshot). non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This clause specifies measurement, scoring, benchmark, or CLI behavior for saved tracker runs; it does not select live operational tracks or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-track-run --adsb <clip.oaf> --out <dir> --realtime [--with-output] [--max-tracks <n>]` offers every report of the clip to the tracker (no split, no scoring; the configuration is `scoring_config` of the full clip, printed with the run) and times each second's updates together with the shell's monotonic clock. It writes `realtime.txt` and `seconds.csv`: for every second from the first to the last, including seconds with no measurements and the last, the measurements, the processing time and the confirmed and tentative track counts after the last update in the second (a second with no updates carries the previous counts; the tracker is not advanced to the second boundary, and the peaks are sampled once per second). It reports the time's p50, p99 and maximum over all those seconds (an empty second counts as zero) and, labelled as such with their count, p50 and p99 over the seconds with at least one measurement; the seconds that did not finish within the second and the longest backlog under this queue model: each second's reports form one batch, available when the second ends, processed during the next second, leftover work carried on (backlog = max(0, backlog + work - 1 s)), a second finishing late when backlog is left, so a report waits at most 1 s plus the backlog ahead of its batch before processing starts and a batch completes at most its own work later (latency at most 1 s + backlog + that second's work), an upper bound because real reports arrive spread through the second; the final advance and flush apart (including the output spill with `--with-output`), CPU and wall time of the update window, which also hold the per-second track-count scan and bookkeeping, next to the sum of the per-second timers and the difference named as outside them (the sum is at most the window) and, read right after the final flush and before any digest, of the run from its start (ingest, set-up, updates, flush) against the traffic's span with the CPU source named (and, when the `/proc/self/stat` fallback served any reading, how many and its assumed 100 Hz tick rate), the conditions (input decoded and held in memory before timing, sorted by time, one thread: the figures exclude network input, decoding and interrupts of a live feed; a second with no measurements does no tick work, its tick rows are emitted with the next update and charged to that second), every refusal and overflow counter, resident memory with the process peak labelled, and the tracker table bytes. A run summary digest (the track log and the counters, taken after the timed window; `oa-track` has no tracker state hash) is always printed; `--with-output` also writes the output rows to column files and prints their digest. These digests are comparable only between realtime runs of the same clip, the same `--max-tracks` and the same build, not with the golden digests of the split, scored run. The run fails (non-zero exit) on an empty clip, on no measurements after the adapter, on any measurement outside the per-second log (no figures are computed over a truncated span), and, after printing its report, on any capacity refusal (not a full-load measurement) and on any lost output row or track log entry (the digests would cover truncated data). `--with-output` and `--max-tracks` need `--realtime`; `--realtime` refuses `--digest`, `--rows`, `--no-score` and `--no-compare`. The per-second log is a pure function of what it is given.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A synthetic path is refused when its start or any knot position is not finite or lies more than 20,037,508 m (half the Earth's circumference) from the plane origin, or when an altitude or vertical rate is past 204,800 ft or 262,144 fpm; no truth is built from it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A latency record whose receive time minus sensor time does not fit a 64-bit integer is refused and counted, not stored with a clamped value.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Once the output table is full, an advance computes no further row: the rows it could not emit (the remaining ticks of each confirmed track, to the tick at which the track is dropped) are counted in the table's overflow count in one pass over the tracks, with no work per tick. One confirmed track, a one-row table, 100 ms ticks and an advance of one hour compute at most two rows (36,001 before) and count exactly the rows left out.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The fusion layer's processing path (queues, ready inputs, per-radar association lists, events, initiation lists, candidates, track records, registration history, assignment log) runs in buffers made at start with named capacities and cleared and reused; a buffer at its capacity refuses and counts. Under three radars, registration, Mode S and radar-only plots over 384 s no such buffer changes address or capacity (a check on the buffers: it does not see a temporary allocated and freed within a call). The two per-key tables (hold runs, registration keys) are among the buffers checked.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tracker, fusion layer and their helpers call no platform maths function in production code (`sin`, `atan2`, `exp`, `ln`, `hypot`, `powi`, `mul_add` and the rest of a fixed list); the elementary functions are `oa-math`'s, so a run is the same bits on every IEEE-754 machine (RULESET B6). The check is itself tested against a planted call.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The `oa-track` run checks the split of the clip with `oa_bench::split_check::check_split` right after `split_reports`; a violation is a hard error of the run. The scorer builds the legacy table by truth leg (the chunk ranges are by address, so all legs of an address are in one chunk).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The fusion layer records where a bucket's work goes and what its work limits leave out: tracks predicted for association, coarse-window width, wide-list tracks and overflow, emitted coarse candidates and visits, exact gate work, polar build/query work and attempted query count, anonymous plots deferred when association work is incomplete, initiation tests and work, the separate bounded initiation-refusal pass visits, and candidates alive at most. Polar work shares `MAX_BUCKET_POLAR_WORK` across all radars in a bucket. `polar_index_query_work` per `polar_index_queries` is charged work per attempted lookup (including a capped lookup); `polar_index_build_work` per `polar_index_track_visits` is charged work per slot visit across the wide-track classification and posting-build passes, including sorting work in the numerator. These are work counters, not elapsed-time or latency measurements. Candidate visits and exact gates share `MAX_BUCKET_TESTS`; neither budget promises an equal per-radar share. Counters are diagnostics and are not read back by the layer.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The scoring split treats reports of one address and time that differ in any field scoring or quality handling reads (`oa_bench::split_check::observation_key`: flags, source, category, SIL type among them) as different observations kept together on one side, in key order; only exact copies are removed. Reversing the input rows changes neither the retained evidence nor the scores. limit was reached, the coarse visits, exact tests and initiation tests, the candidates alive at most and the buckets processed. They are counters only (the layer reads no clock, RULESET B2); none is read back.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A standalone, isolated allocation check runs real tracker and fusion entry points after initialization with an observing global allocator. Its three allocation API controls must be observed, every claimed route has explicit exercise evidence, and any observed allocation, counter overflow, failed control or missing route fails the check. Results name the exercised scope and do not imply coverage of every possible input or real-time crate.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every fusion-study RMS row reports the sample count for each position, speed and heading class. The candidate evaluator refuses missing, empty, malformed or inconsistent class counts. Different variants' emitted primary-track cohorts remain explicit; adding counts never changes the metric's samples, values, thresholds or truth classification.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Starting with `output_new` and using the output append/clear operations, every stored row fills all fifteen columns, preserves prior rows bit for bit (including floating-point payloads), and keeps their lengths equal and within the configured capacity. A full buffer preserves every column and saturating-increments its overflow counter. Clearing empties every column while preserving the configured capacity, accumulated overflow and each column's reserved capacity.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For a per-track report decision whose resulting track is confirmed, an applied, begun or resynced report makes exactly one non-tick row attempt at that report's time and full track address. Each attempt is accounted as a stored row, an explicitly unrepresentable row, or output-capacity overflow. A rejected or unconfirmed report makes no report-row attempt. During late replay only the newly inserted report may produce a report-time row; later replayed history entries do not create backfilled report rows. Tick output is accounted separately. Public lookup, clock admission and held-release behavior retain their own checks.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The coarse query lists each track at most once as it appends, so its output never holds more entries than the index has tracks and a buffer sized for the tracks is never grown, whatever the pieces of the rectangle share (tracks on the boundary of two pieces included); the tracks listed are the same as when the output was sorted and deduplicated afterwards.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This builds or scores synthetic paths and study data; truth labels and evaluation metrics are not tracker runtime inputs.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every pair geometry (crossing and parallel at 3 NM, crossing and same-track at 1,000 ft, and the stress geometries) has its stated closest approach.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every world builds into an exact truth that `oa-bench` accepts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This builds or scores synthetic paths and study data; truth labels and evaluation metrics are not tracker runtime inputs.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The assignment (union-find, component grouping, Hungarian method, greedy fallback, the pair lookup and the ambiguity pass) runs in buffers allocated at start: their addresses and capacities are the same after solves of every shape, and an input with more tracks, plots or pairs than the buffers hold is refused with a typed error (counted by the fusion layer), never grown into. Fusion's own association buffers are likewise unchanged across a run with holds and forced resolutions.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flooded bucket costs a bounded amount: plots of one radar beyond 16,384 in a bucket, pairs beyond the pair limit and exact gate tests beyond the test limit are counted and not processed; the ambiguity and pair-lookup passes are one pass over the pairs, so 20,000 plots over 20,000 tracks are associated in under 3 s in a debug build (the quadratic scans took over 3 s of that alone and grow with the square), and a call that finds no input ready does not scan the queue.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A spill refuses a directory that exists and has anything in it, creates its column files new, and on drop removes only those files (by name) and then the directory if it is empty; a file put into the directory meanwhile survives.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A spill that fails partway through creating its column files removes only the files that call created, and the directory only if that call created it: files another writer made in the same directory survive.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reading a spilled run checks every column file's size against the row count and refuses a truncated or extended column of any of the 15, with a typed error naming the column and the bytes found and expected.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The digest of a spilled run equals the digest of the same rows in memory when rows have no altitude: the altitude columns of such a row hash as zero in both.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A report received before its sensor time is counted as clock skew (`LatencyLog::sensor_negative`); its signed difference is stored as it is.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The runs of the tracker and of the fusion layer on the real ZAU ADS-B clip (radar plots simulated from its trajectories, one and two radars, with and without ADS-B and registration) have fixed output digests: a change of how work is found or bounded does not change what is decided.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tracker run on the same clip, at report times, has a fixed output digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The simulated ADS-B noise of a sample depends only on the seed, the address and the sample's time, so the two legs of one aircraft do not repeat each other's draws and a simulation of a subrange reproduces exactly the samples of the full run that it covers.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ADS-B simulation refuses, before allocating, a reporting period that is zero or negative, a NACp or NACv without a bound, and a run of more than 2^25 samples (a 1 ns period over seconds); the study's one-hour clip at one report per second is 657,824 samples and runs.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A synthetic truth refuses a path whose duration is too long to count (including an infinite sum), a start time that overflows the clock with the epoch, and an origin that is not a finite latitude and longitude, with an error and not a panic.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Interval statistics of measurements at the extremes of the clock, and the fusion tracker configuration for a radar period at the largest value, saturate and do not overflow.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tracker configuration whose output or log table exceeds 2^24 rows is refused; the registration estimator and the association scratch size their buffers at a stated maximum (4,096 reference slots; 2^22 tracks, plots or pairs) whatever is asked for.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reports of one address with the same time and the same position, altitudes, velocity and quality fields are one observation: one copy is kept, the removed copies are counted and shown in the report. The split of [r0,r0,r2,r2,r4,r4] has no observation in both sets.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Duplicating a whole recording gives the same two sets and the same split counts except the number of copies removed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reports of one address and time with different content are a conflict: all stay on the side of the first, and the conflicting times and reports are counted. A row that cannot be read is left out and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The per-flight position RMS is per truth leg: two trips of one address are two flights, so a failing short trip is not pooled with a good long one and counts above the R4 value.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `split_reports_with(r, false)` is the split with the halving off: the same copy removal, conflict handling and quality handling, every distinct report in the first set, the second empty, and the same removal and conflict counts as the halving run.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures or accounts for storage, work, timing, or diagnostics, rather than which aircraft state is selected or whether an alert is issued.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: No order or selection in the tracker reads the sign or payload of a NaN: the greedy order of a component larger than `MAX_COMPONENT` uses `oa_math::cmp_canon_f64`, so positive, negative and payload NaN costs have one canonical order. When a plot has more coarse candidates than its visit allowance, `coarse_distance` maps NaN geometry to zero; the bounded ranking packs the nonnegative distance bits in the high portion and the track index in the low portion, then orders the integer keys. Thus all NaN geometries produce the same selection and ties use track number. Real-data digests are unchanged where no NaN reaches a migrated sort; a sort that does see NaN uses the canonical ordering rather than the NaN sign (OA-TRC-260 keeps raw float-order and sign methods out of non-test workspace sources).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Percentiles are by the nearest-rank rule (the 99.9th of 1,000 values is the 999th), with weights (a call that processed n inputs counts n times) and in a fixed-bin histogram whose maximum, mean and count are exact; a key=value file round-trips.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The synthetic traffic is a pure function of its seed and the second asked for: the same seed gives the same aircraft, ADS-B reports and plots, another seed does not; one ADS-B report per equipped aircraft per second; plots at the scan rates of the radars (12 s en-route, 4.8 s terminal), in time order, inside the second asked for, and valid for the tracker.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A capacity run feeds the traffic to the fusion layer one second at a time, times each advance, and reports the time per second of traffic, the per-advance distribution, every capacity counter, the data age of the rows, the input-to-effect delay and the memory; two runs of one configuration count the same things.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A run that overfills the tracker is refused and counted, not stopped: the refusal counters move and the buffers are the same at the end as at the start.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Memory is read from `/proc/self/status` (`VmHWM`, `VmRSS`) in kilobytes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A latency pass offers every input of a time-ordered feed to the fusion layer and advances it to the input's time, timing each call; it reports the time of every call, of the calls that processed inputs and of those shared over the inputs they processed, and the tracker alone is timed per report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The command line refuses unknown commands, flags and values, and the overload comparison reads the counters of the knee run and the overload run.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every plot of the synthetic traffic is where its aircraft is at the time the plot carries, to within the plot noise; a revolution in which the aircraft crosses the beam's starting azimuth and the crossing cannot be solved gives no plot.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A capacity run passes (`keeps_up`, and the strict knee with it) only if every measured second's advance took under 1 s of wall time and every loss-of-work counter (`loss_counters`: refusals, overflows, capped or ungated association work, full tables and buffers, late and dropped inputs, output rows lost) is zero over the measured window; a run that is fast but loses work is reported as lost work, not a pass. The mean and 99th percentile are reported, not tested. Every counter of the fusion and tracker statistics is listed as loss or as not loss.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The command line refuses a `--max-wall` that is not a positive finite number, an `--adsb-frac` outside 0 to 1, and traffic times (`--warmup`, `--duration`, `--clip-secs`) whose sum overflows or passes the time range the layer accepts, each with a message naming the flag.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every aircraft of the synthetic traffic is inside its box at every second of the fed interval (warm-up plus measurement, up to the traffic's horizon): a track that would leave the box flies the reverse heading, and one that would still leave flies straight to a point from which it turns at the standard rate (3 degrees per second) onto a circle that fits in the box and circles there. Velocity is continuous and of constant magnitude, and no aircraft turns faster than the standard rate. So in the stress layout every aircraft is in the coverage of every radar throughout, no plot is lost to leaving it, and no aircraft makes a manoeuvre a real aircraft could not fly. Deterministic per seed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A capacity run independently counts unique generated truth aircraft offered during measurement, using ADS-B addresses and radar scoring labels in the shell only. All configured aircraft must appear and unknown labels must be zero; repeated sightings count once. Tracker hypothesis count is diagnostic and does not establish input load or distinct aircraft identity.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-perf one --radar-no-altitude` removes Mode C altitude from every generated anonymous radar plot in the measured window, after an unchanged warm-up. It reports the start second and exact number removed. The radar schedule, plot count and truth labels remain unchanged, so a control and degraded run with the same seed exercise identical aircraft and plot times.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies synthetic workload, timing, memory, or refusal measurements; it is evidence, not a runtime performance guarantee or track decision.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Radar conversion refusals retain fixed-size reason counters for every conversion stage, distinguishing missing height, invalid plot, unreachable altitude and numerical geometry failures. These diagnostic subsets preserve existing aggregate loss totals and do not double-count loss or change qualification acceptance thresholds.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This clause records ICD workload estimates and calculations; it does not implement or decide the coordination message/session state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ICD workload figures (Table 29 per-flight counts, Table 3-IV peak rates, the 13.2 RTUs per handoff arithmetic, the latency and size bounds) are carried as data and agree with each other and with the codec's size limits.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-replay-diff` calls two digests identical only when every line, chain hash included, is equal; otherwise it reports the first differing second, the number of differing seconds (a second whose rows differ in hash or count, or that only one run has) and how many seconds only one run has.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A malformed digest file (wrong field count, a number or hash that does not parse, seconds not strictly increasing) is an error naming the line, and the tool exits 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Given both rows files, for each differing second the tool reports the rows added, removed and changed (rows matched by track address, time, tick flag and order among equals), the tracks affected, the changed rows by class (position, velocity, covariance, flags, model), the largest absolute difference of every field over finite values, the count of changed non-finite values, and the flag bits that differ; a second whose rows are equal and only reordered is reported as reordered. Totals follow, and a `key=value` summary.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: With an expect file naming the declared classes (`position`, `velocity`, `covariance`, `flags`, `model`, `added`, `removed`, `order`), a difference is accepted (exit 0) only if every class present is declared; an undeclared class, or an expect file without rows files to tell the classes, is a failure (exit 1 or 2), and an unknown class name is an error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A rows file with a wrong magic, version or row size, truncated, not grouped by ascending second, or whose row counts disagree with its digest file is an error (exit 2), never a comparison.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `tools/replay_compare.sh` accepts only commit hashes or refs of the repository, refuses a working-tree or option-like spec, builds each commit in its own clean detached worktree, one build at a time, and records both commits and the clip's SHA-256 in its report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tracker tick row becomes the values of one record in the LSBs of the specification: position in counts of 180/2^25 degree (I062/105), velocity in 0.25 m/s east and north (I062/185), barometric altitude in 1/4 FL (I062/135, no QNH correction), vertical rate in 6.25 ft/min (I062/220), time in 1/128 s since midnight UTC (I062/070), each rounded to nearest. An ERAM sample becomes position, time, velocity (0.1 kt to 0.25 m/s) and the reported altitude as a measured flight level (I062/136).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The time of a row is rounded to 1/128 s and the UTC day is that of the rounded time: a row within 1/256 s before midnight is on the next day with time of day 0, never at 24:00:00. A date is checked against the calendar (leap years, month lengths) and the day count and its inverse agree.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A value a row does not have, or that does not fit its item (not a number, outside -15 FL to 1500 FL, outside the 16-bit velocity or climb range), is left out of the record, never replaced by zero or clipped, and is named in the row's notes; the shell counts each note per system and day and the README lists the counts. A row whose latitude or longitude is out of range, or whose time does not convert, is refused and counted, not written.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: I062/500 subfield 3 (APW) of an OpenATCA row is the standard deviation of the position in latitude and in longitude from the position covariance: `sqrt(nn)` and `sqrt(ee)` metres over the WGS-84 meridian radius and over the prime vertical radius times the cosine of the latitude, in counts of 180/2^25 degree, rounded to nearest; a component of 0 counts is raised to 1 and one past 65 535 is the maximum, each noted; a covariance that is negative or not a number leaves the item out. ERAM rows carry no I500 and say so.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: I062/080 has CNF 0 (confirmed) and SIM, SPI, MON, MRH, SRC at 0; a coasting row adds the three extents with CST (bit 8 of the third) set and an OpenATCA radar-disagrees row sets AFF (bit 4 of the first). The row flags `O_UNCERTAIN` and `O_REACQUIRED`, which CAT062 has no field for, are not encoded and are counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: I062/380 carries the target address only for a 24-bit Mode S address (a track keyed by a radar handle or a non-ICAO address has none, noted) and, for ERAM, the callsign as an identification only if every character is `A-Z`, `0-9` or space (NUL padding becomes spaces); no other character is changed or dropped. I060, I200, I290 and I295 are never written, and counted as omitted on every row.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Encoding then decoding with the `oa-asterix` decoder gives records equal to those encoded, for generated rows of both systems and for the tick rows of the tracker run on a slice of a real recording (skipped when the recording is absent); the decoded position differs from the source position by at most 27 units of 1e-7 degree.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A data block holds at most 256 records, a record is at most 49 octets (every item present), so a block is at most 12 547 octets, under the 65 535 a LEN holds; the encoder refuses a block over it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A file holds one UTC day. Without `--split-days` a row on another day than the one asked for refuses the export (E5) and no file is left behind; with it, one directory per day holds `openatca.ast`, `eram.ast`, `data_sources.json` and `README.txt`, and no file holds a row of another day.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Track numbers (I062/040) are assigned per file in order of first appearance, from 1, one per key and stable over the file; more than 65 535 distinct keys in a file is a refusal, not a wrap.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Records in a file are in non-decreasing I070; a record earlier than the one before it is refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: ERAM samples are sorted by position time, flight and input order; a sample with the same flight, position time and content as an earlier one is dropped and counted, one with different content is kept and counted as a conflict, and a sample whose flight is not in the flight table is counted and not written.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every finished file is read back from disk with the decoder and must hold exactly the records and octets written, with the right data source and time order; a truncated or altered file fails the export.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `data_sources.json` is `{"content_type":"data_sources","content_version":"0.2","data_sources":[...]}` with one `Tracker` entry per system, OpenATCA (SAC 255, SIC 11) and ERAM (SAC 255, SIC 12), and one `ADSB` entry, ADS-B (SAC 255, SIC 13), which parses as JSON. The SAC is a test pair of this export, stated as such in the documentation and the README.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The README states the UTC date to give at import, the SAC/SIC of each system, the items of each file with the rows that carry them, the rows written, every omission and note by reason with its count, the inputs, the I500 conversion and the encoder build.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tracker run behind the OpenATCA file is the scorer's: set A of the split, the scoring configuration, one tick row per second per confirmed track; update rows are not exported and are counted; a run that lost rows to a full output table is refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every count the SFDPS ingest keeps of what it saw and dropped (documents, refusals, rows without a GUFI or position time or position column, rows past the document table, field errors, coast and altitude counts) is printed in the README's ERAM block with its reason, and the export is refused if the flight table or the track-sample table overflowed (rows were lost). Counters saturate, and an index that does not fit a `u32` is a refusal, not a truncation.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--inputs all` (default) offers the OpenATCA tracker's adapter every ADS-B report of the clip, `--inputs split` only set A of the scorer's split; the README states the mode, whether the two files are like-for-like, and, for `split`, that a reference built from set A would be leaked truth. I062/080 MON is 1 for OpenATCA (ADS-B only) and 0 for ERAM; the README says why. ERAM altitude, whose reference the feed does not state, is I136 at or above 18 000 ft and I135 with QNH = 1 below, stated in the README as an inference. A valid rate of climb is exported on a row without an altitude and counted; a longitude of +180 degrees is written as -180 and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: One ADS-B report converts to the counts of CAT021 Ed 2.4's items exactly as the item definitions give them: I073 (1/128 s), I131 (180/2^30 degrees), I080, I145 (1/4 FL), I140 (6.25 ft), I155 or I157 (6.25 ft/min, by the report's rate flag), I160 (2^-14 NM/s, 360/2^16 degrees), I170, I020, I090, I210 and I040 (ATP, GBS, CL 2); a full report (every I090 field known) notes only what the source never has.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: What a report lacks, or has outside the range of its item (FL -15 to 1500, height -1500 to 150 000 ft, vertical rate 15 bits, a track of 360 degrees, a character outside A-Z 0-9 space, an emitter category without an I020 code, MOPS version 3), is left out of the record and counted by item and reason; nothing is clipped.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A non-ICAO address is written with ATP 3, a ground report sets GBS and has no flight level, a field that does not fit its bits counts as unknown, a callsign padded with NUL is the callsign padded with spaces (a NUL inside it is refused), and the emitter categories map to the I020 codes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A position beyond 90 or 180 degrees refuses the report; +180 degrees is written as -180 and counted; the position error is at most 1 unit of 1e-7 degree; a time within 1/256 s before midnight belongs to the next day.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `adsb.ast` decodes with the Ed 2.4 decoder to the values converted; every block is decoded again before it is written and the file is read back from disk; reports are written in time order, and stale positions and source types that are not ADS-B are left out and counted. The README reconciles the reports offered with stale, not ADS-B, written and refused ("reconciles" or "DOES NOT RECONCILE").

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A report earlier than the one before it, or on another UTC day than the requested one, refuses the export unless days are split, which writes one directory per day.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--inputs all` runs the clip through `oa_track::score::split_reports_with` (the scorer's split function) with the halving off: copies removed, every conflicting report kept (rule stated), counts printed in the README; the same reports are offered to the tracker's adapter and to `adsb.ast`; the tracker uses the subset that passes its quality gates (OA-CMP-028).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `data_sources.json` lists the ADS-B source (SAC 255, SIC 13, DSType "ADSB", a string of the COMPASS manual's set); the README states the Ed 2.4 format, how each value was made, every omission with its count, and that a reference built from `adsb.ast` is not independent of OpenATCA's inputs (UK-008) and that ERAM also uses ADS-B.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-compass slice --in DIR --from HH:MM:SS --to HH:MM:SS --out DIR2` reads each `.ast` file with the decoder (CAT062 Ed 1.21, CAT021 Ed 2.4), keeps the records with I070 or I073 in [from, to), writes them again unchanged in verified blocks, reads each file back, copies `data_sources.json` and writes a README with the window, the source directory and the records in and kept per file; a window across midnight or empty, a category other than 21 and 62, and a damaged file are refused, leaving no partial file.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: I021/090 is in every ADS-B record (Ed 2.4 5.2.16, Encoding Rule: "This item shall be present in every ASTERIX record. Extensions are sent only if at least 1 bit is set to 1", quoted from the specification text used). Its primary subfield is always written: an unknown NACv or NIC is the MOPS code 0 (unknown), each counted; NIC is readsb's value written as NUCp/NIC, and under MOPS version 2 it is written unchanged with the mapping UNVERIFIED and each row counted; for version 0 the NUCp is written 0 and counted (readsb's `nic` is a NIC) and the NUCr (the NACv field) is written 0 whatever the report's NACv holds, counted as "NUCr not available" and not as an unknown NACv; a version 0 row is never mapped through the NUCp column of the PIC table. Beyond the primary subfield no zero stands in for a missing value: each extension (first NICBARO, SIL, NACp; second SILS, SDA, GVA; third PIC) is written only while every field in it and in those before it is known, the chain stops at the first extension with an unknown field and the rows cut short are counted per extension; an all-zero extension is sent only before a later one that has bits, so a decoder cannot tell a known 0 from an extension not sent. NICBARO is the clip's NIC_baro (a clip written before the column carries none). PIC is taken from NIC and the MOPS version (1 or 2) by the Ed 2.4 table (`pic_of`; NIC 6 gives none; PIC 0 is never generated), is written when the chain reaches it, and rows for which it cannot be taken are counted. NIC or NACp above 11 and NACv above 4 are not encoded and count as unknown. I040 GBS is 1 when the report says ground and 0 when it carries an altitude (an inference from readsb); a row with neither is written GBS 0 and counted as "ground state unknown"; ARC, CL, RC, RAB, DCR, SIM, TST and SAA are defaults, listed in the README as defaults and not facts. I210 LTT is 2 for the source types adsb_icao and adsb_icao_nt (ASSUMED from the source type, not proven: such a report can come through a UAT-to-ES converter), 1 for a UAT source (the clip's types have none), and 0, counted, for a clip without the source type column or for adsb_other; the source types mlat, tisb_*, adsr_*, mode_s and the rest are not ADS-B reports, are not written and are counted by source type. The I090 and I210 octets are checked against bytes worked out by hand from the specification. I160 is omitted on a ground report and counted; the README states that adsb.ast is a superset of what the tracker was fed, with the tracker adapter's removals per reason, and keeps the independence statement (UK-008).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The three data sources are SAC 255 with SIC 11 (OpenATCA), 12 (ERAM) and 13 (ADS-B), one constant each; 255/1 is left free because COMPASS writes its reference there, and the README says so.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The export refuses an `--out` that exists and is not empty (the same rule as `slice`), before anything is written. The README lists exactly the files this run wrote into its directory, and its title, import instruction, data-source entries and system paragraphs follow which systems were exported (OpenATCA, ERAM, ADS-B): an ERAM-only run's README does not mention `openatca.ast`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The position error limit is enforced: when a decoded position differs from its source by more than `MAX_POSITION_ERROR_E7` (27 for CAT062, 1 for CAT021) the export fails with a verification error and no file is committed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every README claim about the rows is backed by code: the tracker's `O_IDENTITY_UNCONFIRMED` rows are counted and written with CNF = 0 (the flag means an unconfirmed identity, not a tentative track, and the README says so); MON = 0 and CNF = 0 for ERAM are stated as assumptions ("not in the feed") and counted as a note on every ERAM row; each system's README section states the nature of its rows and the measured interval between consecutive rows of one track (median, 90th percentile, longest, pairs), computed by code; ERAM track numbers are the export's own (one per flight) and the flights per address are counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The commit the README names is embedded at build time (`build.rs`, `git -C` the crate's own directory, with a note if tracked files are modified), `unknown` only if git is unavailable at build.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The main export commits like `slice`: every file (data, `data_sources.json`, README) is written as `.partial`, all are renamed in one pass, and on any error every file this run created is removed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every ERAM flight with an address is checked against the ADS-B reports of the same address (nearest report within 10 s, at least 10 pairs, median distance over 25 km contradicts; the rule and its reason are in the README); the check is report-only by default (`--eram-contradicted-address keep`: the address ERAM published is written, a contradicting flight is counted and listed with its evidence); with `drop` the contradicting flight is written without I380 address and the README says the file was altered and lists the flights; a flight with too few pairs is counted as not checked in both modes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--openatca-rows ticks|updates` (default `ticks`, unchanged) selects the tracker's one-second tick rows or its update rows (one per applied report, at the report's time, earlier-than-written rows counted and left out); the README states the mode prominently and counts the rows of the other kind.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
