non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The native regression guard passes only with hash-verified result and log artifacts, matching source identity, the exact pinned test command and a one-test successful log summary.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines set-level scoring and synthetic study accounting; it does not make operational identity decisions.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Candidate and frozen-default builds share the same source head and runner, have parameter-source bytes differing only at the registered `H_Q_CV` declaration, bind a source diff limited to that declaration, and both carry passing native regression evidence.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines set-level scoring and synthetic study accounting; it does not make operational identity decisions.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Run manifests use the frozen `adsb_kinematic_v2` model for the six established scenarios and `adsb_motion_study_v1` only for onset-exit.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines set-level scoring and synthetic study accounting; it does not make operational identity decisions.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Onset-exit truth validation compares geographic velocity using the WGS84 Jacobian at each generated latitude while retaining the frozen position and velocity tolerances.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines set-level scoring and synthetic study accounting; it does not make operational identity decisions.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Containment uses position error in candidate-local ENU axes matching emitted covariance, and turn-rate residuals use the tracker's clockwise-positive sign convention.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This defines set-level scoring and synthetic study accounting; it does not make operational identity decisions.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The motion-study scorer, selector and checker load `validation/motion-study-v1.json` only if its bytes match the pinned v1 SHA-256, and otherwise fail closed with "protocol file does not match the frozen v1 hash".

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `tools/replay_compare.sh` reads from each commit's tree, before any build, the digest format it will emit (the header constant of its `canon.rs`, or v2 for a commit that gets the overlay); a commit that would emit v1, a half-way commit (only one of `canon.rs` and `--digest`) or an unknown header is exit 2. It runs both `oa-track-run` calls in the same `env -i` environment as the builds, and records the diff tool's build commit and whether that tree was clean in the report and in `summary.txt`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This compares saved outputs for regression analysis; the result does not feed back into operational state.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Replay witness comparison accepts two guarded regular files containing only the versioned settings, complete ordered-input, and final-state lines. Each file is limited to 4 KiB. Positive frame counts and zero refusal counters are required. The verdict checks settings first, then admitted frame count and ordered-input digest, then final-state digest.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The sealed hold-out day (2026-11-19, one named constant) is never exported: `--date` of it is refused in every date syntax. Any input path the shared sealed list refuses (`oa-sealed`, OA-SEAL-001), and every file the run opens (each file of the feed directory, the ADS-B clip, each file and the README of a `slice` source), is checked as given and after resolving links and opened through the shared guard; a path that cannot be resolved is refused. `--out` of a run or of `slice` is refused in the same way (the nearest existing ancestor of a path yet to be created is resolved). `slice` refuses a source whose README import date is the sealed day, or has no readable date line. Limits: a hard link, copy, rename or bind mount of a sealed file has no sealed component in its path and is not detectable by path, which is why OA-CMP-051 exists. A flag value that starts with `--` is a missing value and a repeated flag is an error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A track restart gets a new I062/040 number, from the tracker's own end events and not from gaps between exported rows: a confirmed track instance the tracker dropped is logged with its last applied update; a row of that address later than that time plus the drop age (`oa_track::score::SCORE_DROP_AFTER_NS`) is of a later instance, exact to the nanosecond, in ticks and updates mode, also when both instances' rows are in one batch. The tracker holds one live track per address (one slot per key). A full track log fails the run. Any `time_steps_back` or `time_future_dropped` above zero fails the run, whether or not a confirmed track was dropped, because the tracks a step back drops at once ended at the step and not at their last update plus the drop age; the failure leaves nothing under `--out` (tests `a_tracker_clock_step_back_fails_the_run_instead_of_misplacing_a_restart`, `a_step_back_on_the_very_last_measurement_fails_the_run`, `a_step_back_before_any_track_was_confirmed_still_fails_the_run`; the ADS-B inputs of a job are sorted by time before the tracker, so a step back is not reachable through `run_job`). The row pair that spans a restart is left out of the interval statistics, and the README counts restarts. ERAM rows use one track number per flight.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Track numbers are one per (key, segment), allocated in order of first appearance, refused when the 16-bit space (65 535 numbers, restarts included) is exhausted; the README gives track segments, keys, keys with more than one segment and the numbers used of the 65 535 available.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: I062/185 Vx and Vy are the true east and north velocity at the target (the frame of the CAT062 specification and of COMPASS); the README names the frame for OpenATCA only. For ERAM the README says the frame is as the feed gives it and not verified. Each sentence is printed only when its system is present.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This specifies an offline CAT062/CAT021 export artifact; no live publication or operational consumer is established.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Before any directory or file is created and before the tracker runs, every raw input time (every ADS-B report of the clip including stale and other-source ones, every ERAM sample including unknown-flight, duplicate and refused ones) is checked: one on the sealed day by its raw time or once rounded to 1/128 s (the day the export would file it under) refuses the run, naming the system and the count, with nothing created. The tracker's rows and every pushed row are checked again at the push. Records the clip loader itself drops as undecodable are not reports and cannot be checked. The count of rows and frames the readers dropped in a sealed window is given on every exit of the run, a refusal in the pre-scan or a failure after it included. `oa-compass slice` reads the day from the source README (none, or one that does not parse, is a refusal), computes each record's absolute time from that day and its time of day, tests it against the sealed day and the sealed windows and, in a file whose time of day goes back (midnight wrapped), on the day after as well; if any record of any file could be sealed the whole slice is refused with a non-zero exit, and the drop line is printed on every exit.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Flights are paired by exactly one rule. An ERAM flight with a Mode S address that OpenATCA has an aircraft for pairs with that aircraft. Any other ERAM flight with a beacon code pairs with the OpenATCA aircraft that is not already paired (by address or by beacon) to an ERAM flight whose span overlaps this one's (beacon claims are exclusive within overlapping spans), was offered the code within the flight's span plus 30 s, and is nearest to ERAM's first in-box, in-window report of the flight within 5 NM (ties to the lowest address). The code is the one in force at that first report, or the earliest if the first message came later. Several ERAM flights of one aircraft form one group.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight or aircraft with no partner is a difference (`UNPAIRED_ERAM`, `UNPAIRED_OA`) with its first and last time and duration and its own row in the flight table; it is not dropped.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: At each ERAM report time the raw cross-track and along-track separations from OpenATCA are judged separately: above 0.5 NM (926 m) and up to 1 NM (1852 m) is `POS_*_0P5_TO_1NM`, above 1 NM is `POS_*_GT_1NM`; a separation exactly at a threshold is not in the class above it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: ERAM stamps whole seconds. The classification uses the raw along-track separation; the event carries OpenATCA's ground speed times 1 s (`along_credit_m`) and a flag `within_1s_stamp_allowance`, true when the raw separation less that credit is not over the event's threshold; the summary counts the events with and without the flag. Cross-track events carry no flag. Below 2 kt the direction is undefined and the whole separation counts as cross-track.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: OpenATCA is linearly interpolated to the ERAM report time between two of its one-second rows at most 2 s apart, or taken from the row at that time; with no such rows it has no sample there.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An altitude difference above 300 ft either way is `ALT_GT_300FT`, only where both systems have an altitude; the others are counted as not comparable. Each event names the band of ERAM's altitude (below or at or above 18,000 ft), and the summary gives the event counts and the median signed difference of both bands (no altimeter setting is applied).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Identity: a report disagrees on the beacon when ERAM's code in force (each message's code carried forward) differs from every squawk the OpenATCA adapter was offered within +-60 s of the report time (inclusive, the one in force at the window start included); a disagreement counts only when it lasts at least 3 consecutive reports of the ERAM flight, and each such run is one `ID_BEACON` event with its span (the first report's codes in the detail). Nothing is compared where either side has no code, and a report that agrees or is not compared ends a run. `ID_CALLSIGN` is the same for ERAM's callsign against the callsigns offered (case and padding ignored).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A paired aircraft's first compared ERAM report and OpenATCA's first in-box row (and the last of each) differ by more than 12 s plus the ERAM report interval at that end: `START_TIMING`, `DROP_TIMING`, with the direction. Gaps inside the track are `ERAM_REPORT_GAP` only. The summary prints the median ERAM report interval.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: ERAM reports with no OpenATCA sample are `ERAM_ONLY_SPAN` (consecutive reports one span); OpenATCA rows outside the span of every ERAM flight of the aircraft, each widened by 12 s plus the report interval at that end, are `OA_ONLY_SPAN` (consecutive rows one span). A span's duration is first to last plus half the local sample interval at each end (a lone sample gets one interval; an interval counts at most 30 s).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Where ERAM has a report and OpenATCA has a row at exactly that time, ERAM flagging coast and OpenATCA not is `COAST_ERAM_ONLY` and the reverse is `COAST_OA_ONLY`; the flag is not interpolated and the summary says the two flags are different concepts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: With truth, each position event also names which system was closer to the truth at the ERAM report time (`ERAM`, `OpenATCA`, `tie` within 1 m, or empty without truth), computed after classification. The events, their order and values are the same with and without truth. The summary states that the truth shares its source with OpenATCA's input and favours OpenATCA, and counts the truth queries that gave no answer.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report is deterministic: `events.csv`, `flights.csv` and `summary.txt` are byte-identical for the same inputs; the summary holds no path, clock or run time and ends with a digest line over the three texts; it counts every class (events, flights, span, largest) and gives no aircraft address or callsign. A value that rounds to zero is written without a sign.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The thresholds are one table and the summary prints every one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The flight table has one row per group and per unpaired flight or aircraft, with a flight index (the only name in the summary), the compared count and the worst cross-track, along-track and altitude difference.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Both systems are restricted to the clip box (38.5 to 46.5 N, 83.5 to 93.5 W, inclusive); the identity the adapter was offered is the squawk and callsign carried forward from the aircraft's reports, one point per change.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An input or output path the shared sealed list refuses (OA-SEAL-001), as given or after resolving links, is refused before anything is opened, exit 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A missing, repeated, unknown or valueless flag (a value starting with `--` is missing) is a usage error, exit 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The two recordings are cut to the overlap of their in-box recorded extents (ERAM's in-box track positions, OpenATCA's rows) before anything is compared, edges inclusive; a flight or aircraft left with no samples is gone, and the summary states the window in UTC. Recordings that do not overlap are an error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A gap of more than 30 s between two reports of one ERAM flight is `ERAM_REPORT_GAP` with its length; OpenATCA rows inside the flight's span are not `OA_ONLY_SPAN`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two ERAM flights of one aircraft with overlapping spans: the overlap is `DUP_ERAM_TRACK` (its duration, the union of the overlap with the flights before it in priority), and a flight's reports inside the segments of those flights (gaps over 30 s not covered) are not compared; the flight with the earliest first report (ties: the lower flight index) is the primary. Each (aircraft, ERAM time) is compared once.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An address-paired ERAM flight more than 20 NM from the paired aircraft for 3 or more consecutive reports is `ADDR_CONTRADICTS_TRACK` (with the span) and its reports in the span are left out of the position classes and of the worst-case columns.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every file the run opens is canonicalised and refused when it resolves into a sealed recording, so a link inside an unsealed directory is caught; the run itself checks its arguments before creating anything.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A start or drop difference is not reported as `START_TIMING`/`DROP_TIMING` where an `OA_ONLY_SPAN` or `ERAM_ONLY_SPAN` already covers the interval between the two times; the span classes are disjoint by construction and the summary says span totals add.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `DUP_ERAM_TRACK` is one event per secondary flight, its value the union of overlap time with the primary flights; a secondary's reports inside a gap of over 30 s of the primary are compared.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `ERAM_REPORT_GAP` is measured on the compared (not duplicate-excluded) reports only.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A beacon-paired flight is measured against the OpenATCA row nearest its first report within 12 s plus the ERAM report interval, else the first row inside its span; no interpolated sample is needed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Reports in an `ADDR_CONTRADICTS_TRACK` span are also left out of altitude, coast and identity; a report with no OpenATCA sample neither extends nor breaks a contradiction run.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An output path that does not exist yet is resolved through its nearest existing ancestor before the sealed check.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This computes recorded-feed differences without feeding results back into fusion or alerts.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every nonzero load count is printed in the summary header; a beacon table that overflowed (`DROP_SFDPS_BEACON_FULL`) fails the run.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A pair is in a class when its horizontal separation is strictly under the class's horizontal limit and its vertical separation strictly under the vertical limit; the record volume has the same strict edges, and the class of a finished encounter is the tightest class any tick with a known altitude met.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An encounter starts at the first tick a pair is inside the record volume and ends when the pair has been outside it for the hysteresis (end time the last tick inside); a re-entry within the hysteresis continues the same encounter and a later one is a new encounter.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each encounter records the time of the closest horizontal approach, the minimum horizontal separation, the vertical separation and the mean altitude at that time, the minimum scaled three-dimensional separation, both tracks' flags and whether either was on the ground at that time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A pair with both aircraft on the ground inside the record volume is not recorded and is counted; one aircraft on the ground, or an unknown ground state, is recorded.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A pair inside the horizontal radius with an altitude unknown on either track is recorded by horizontal distance, and an encounter with no tick of known altitude is class ALT_UNKNOWN; none is dropped.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The grid scan and the pair evaluation count their work against configured budgets; over budget the pairs are evaluated in order of smallest separation, the remainder is counted as not evaluated, an open encounter whose pair was not evaluated is kept alive and marked, and every shortfall (tracks not scanned, candidates dropped, encounters not opened) is a count.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The record is a deterministic function of the rows: the same rows in any order give the same encounters and counts; rows sharing an address, or with no valid position, are left out and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The grid finds every pair that the exact separation test finds inside the record radius, including across the antimeridian and at high and southern latitudes up to the limit `atan(0.02 / dphi)` (`dphi` the radius over 6,356,752 m, 85.8 degrees for 5 NM), which the core reports; rows above it are used and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool refuses, with exit 2 and before opening or creating anything, an input or output path that is, is inside, or resolves (through a link or the nearest existing ancestor of a new directory) into a sealed 2026-11-19 recording; its arguments are strict.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A cycle whose time is not after the previous cycle's is refused and counted, an out-of-range configuration is refused, and a full encounter log counts what it loses.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool writes `encounters.csv` and `summary.txt` deterministically, sorted by start time; the summary has counts per class, altitude band, hour and 0.25 degree cell, the work and overflow counts, a degraded state when any shortfall is non-zero and the digest of `encounters.csv`, and contains no aircraft address.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A synthetic close pass run through the tracker and the record gives one encounter of the expected class and distance, repeats exactly, is not recorded at a large vertical separation, and the on-ground state at a tick is the latest report not older than 30 s.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The true minimum horizontal separation of an encounter is found by moving the pair's relative position in a straight line between two consecutive ticks that were both evaluated, and its time is recorded beside the sampled minimum, which is kept; the interpolated minimum is never above the sampled one, and no line is drawn across a tick that was not evaluated. The smallest vertical separation and the vertical rates at the closest approach and their largest magnitude are recorded.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each encounter has one context at its closest approach: SURFACE (either aircraft on the ground, or within 5 NM of a public airport and under the field elevation plus 200 ft), else DEGRADED_TRACK (either track coasting or uncertain), else AIRBORNE (both altitudes known) or AIRBORNE_ALT_UNKNOWN; the distance classes apply within each context.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The summary leads with AIRBORNE and then AIRBORNE_ALT_UNKNOWN, counts SURFACE and DEGRADED_TRACK with the rule that defines each, lists every encounter at or above 18,000 ft pressure altitude without an address with its breakdown (vertical at the level of 975 ft or more, a climb or descent, anything else), and gives the AIRBORNE vertical separation at the closest approach from 900 to 1,000 ft in 25 ft bins.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For an encounter at or above 18,000 ft the tool finds the smallest separation between the two aircraft's own reports (one aircraft's position at the other's report times, straight between its reports when under 30 s apart (the clip's reports are about 20 s apart at altitude)) during the encounter, and reports none for a pair with no such time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An AIRBORNE encounter whose vertical separation at the closest approach is at least the record volume's vertical limit less one 25 ft altitude quantum, with both vertical rates known and under 300 fpm, is AT_VERTICAL_MINIMUM: it stays in the record and the CSV (a column), is counted on its own line with its rule and is left out of the AIRBORNE class, band and hour tables.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The airports of the surface rule are the NASR `APT_BASE.csv` rows of site type airport and public use, with position and field elevation, read from the CSV archive; a missing file or a bad archive is an error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A shortfall never ends or splits an encounter: when the candidate table overflowed, or rows were removed (a duplicate address, no valid position, over capacity), every open encounter not evaluated at the tick whose pair could have been lost to it is kept alive and its unevaluated ticks counted; the counts add up (`evaluated + not_evaluated = candidates`, the dropped ones a part of `not_evaluated`), and a hysteresis of zero or less is refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The grid skips, and counts, a pair whose two altitudes are known and not under the record volume's vertical limit apart (strict, as the volume test); an unknown altitude is never skipped, and the record is the same as without the skip.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This creates post-hoc encounter records and completeness diagnostics; it does not issue a live warning or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The core states the latitude limit of the grid test, rows above it are counted, and the summary prints both and calls the record degraded when any is non-zero, as for duplicate and invalid rows.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-shadow screen` compares ADS-B with ERAM's reports of address-paired aircraft: ADS-B is evaluated at each ERAM report time by oa-truth's smoother (default settings) and the offset ADS-B minus ERAM is resolved along and across the ADS-B velocity direction. The along offset is `c - L x speed`: L is the apparent latency, positive when ADS-B is late (a late report is behind); b is the mean cross offset, positive to the right. A known injected latency and offset are recovered within the bootstrap interval.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two stages, because one aircraft's speed barely varies and its c and L are collinear: (a) the fleet fit of c and L over all samples of the screened aircraft, by Theil-Sen (the reference: all pairs of 12 evenly spaced samples of each aircraft, the same for the point fit and every bootstrap resample; a bootstrap over aircraft for its interval) and by least squares (pulled by lagged aircraft); (b) per aircraft L_i alone, the median of (c_fleet - along) / speed, and its latency excess L_i - fleet L; the cross offset b is the median cross offset. A constant along-track offset and a latency are indistinguishable at constant speed, so a constant-speed aircraft is identified only through stage (b). The two-parameter per-aircraft fit is a cross-check for aircraft whose speed (5th to 95th percentile) spans 50 kt or more. Aircraft are listed by ascending address.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: LAG is the lower 95 % bound of the latency excess strictly over 0.1 s, meaning an along-track excess equivalent to a latency of 0.1 s or more; EARLY is the upper bound strictly under -0.1 s (counted, not a LAG). BIAS is |b - fleet cross reference| (the reference: the median of the aircraft's median cross offsets) strictly over max(3 x the 95 % bound of the aircraft's median NACp, the fleet's p95 of |b - reference|) with the lower 95 % bound of it strictly over it too; an unknown NACp never flags BIAS. A LAG or BIAS stays only if the aircraft recomputed without the one sample that most supports it still has it; the counts before and after are printed. LAG is also given with c at both ends of the Theil-Sen c interval and under the least-squares fleet fit.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The aircraft interval is a block bootstrap (blocks of 10 consecutive samples, circular starts, 1000 resamples) seeded from the aircraft address, the fleet interval a seeded bootstrap over aircraft (200 resamples), so two runs give identical values; the valid replicates behind each interval are printed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A sample needs a smoother state, |ADS-B - ERAM| at most 2000 m, a direction of travel (over 2 kt), a 95 % horizontal radius of at most 15 m, a turn rate (heading change over 2 s either side) of at most 0.5 deg/s, a vertical rate of at most 500 ft/min in magnitude (edges kept) and finite offsets; an ERAM report is left out for the first reason that applies, in that order, and every reason is counted. No gap rule applies: a thinned ADS-B trace still gives samples; the distance of a used sample to the nearest raw report is printed. An unknown ERAM altitude has its own band code.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Left out of the screen and counted: ERAM reports in a duplicate-track overlap (a flight lends its span only over the reports that survive the contradiction rule), in a contradicted address span (3 or more consecutive reports over 20 NM from the smoother), and coasted ones; the reasons of OA-SHD-034; the counts add up to the ERAM reports.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Two minimums, both printed: the fleet fit and cross reference use every aircraft with 30 or more samples over 10 minutes or more; only aircraft with 100 or more samples (ten blocks) over 10 minutes or more are screened for flags, and every prevalence line is over those. Aircraft out of the fit are counted under their reason; an aircraft eligible for flags that cannot be screened is an error, so screened equals eligible; with fewer than 30 screened the summary says the day has too few long, gated tracks for a prevalence estimate.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The screen summary carries the fixed caveat text and the statement that an offset and a latency are indistinguishable at constant speed, the fleet c and L with intervals, the BIAS threshold rule and both its terms, the counts and fractions of LAG, BIAS and EARLY, the distributions (p05, p50, p95) and a digest over `aircraft.csv` and the summary; the summary names no address.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a recorded-data comparator; its diagnostics do not feed back into tracking or alerting.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The screen reads only usable raw ADS-B positions (not stale, not on the ground, an ADS-B source, a non-zero latitude), one per millisecond per address, with the NACp carried forward from the last known value (1 to 15) within the truth configuration's carry age; an absent or zero NACp is unknown.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The update interval of a TAIS track is the difference of consecutive `mrtTime` values of one track segment (a run of one key, facility, `recSTARSSrcID` and `trackNum`, that no restart has cut; see OA-CEN-019; a coasting, pseudo or frozen update takes part in the time state, so a coast keeps a segment alive across a gap, since STARS kept the track), attributed to the `adsb` flag of the update that ends it, kept in 10 ms bins to 120 s; the census prints per flag the count, median, 10th and 90th percentile and a histogram in 0.5 s bins to 15 s with the count at 15 s and over.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Flag changes within a track segment are counted (total, segments with one, segments by number of changes), and for each direction the interval across the change, the one before it and the one after it are distributions of their own; intervals across a change stay out of the per-flag distributions.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For the updates of each flag the census counts the share carrying a Mode S address, a Mode 3/A code, code 1200, a callsign, any flight plan field, address with code, and none of address, code and callsign, plus the share with the new flag (the identity shares leave out pseudo, frozen and coasting updates, OA-CEN-021); and the track segments whose adsb=false updates ever carried an address.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every count and distribution is also kept per source facility (the message `src`); a track number at two facilities, or under two `recSTARSSrcID`, is two tracks. A record with neither `src` nor `recSTARSSrcID` is in a facility printed "facility unknown", not a merged all-zero source id; with no `src`, the record's `recSTARSSrcID` names the facility.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An update with no `adsb` element is counted apart (never as false); updates with no `mrtTime`, with a time before the track's previous one, or with a gap over 120 s (a reset) are counted and make no interval; a record with no `trackNum` is counted and not tracked; a frame cut short or a gzip file that ends inside a member (a recording still being written) is counted, never fatal. A damaged gzip file is counted and the run exits 3 after printing the report, as stalled bytes do.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The output holds counts, shares and distributions only: no position, address, callsign, code, flight-plan content or individual time; the only text from the data is a source id of letters and digits, and the only times are the start (rounded down) and end (rounded up) to the second of the STDDS recording and of the ADS-B clip, which are the span of each recording and not the time of any aircraft. Every path (the directory, the ADS-B clip, each subdirectory before it is listed, each file before and after it is opened) goes through the shared guard (OA-SEAL-001), as given and with links resolved, and a sealed one is refused, naming the path (exit 2). A capture day directory is read from its `rec/stdds` folder and only files named `scds-stdds-*`; a day or `rec` directory with no `rec/stdds` is refused (exit 2).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Track segments (not track numbers: STARS reuses them, so one key holds many aircraft) are classed by the flags seen on them (fewer than two flagged updates, all adsb=false, all adsb=true, mixed), with their update counts and per-flag interval distributions. Class, flag counts, changes, change bins, segments with adsb=false, false address counts and the cross-check by class are all taken per segment; the report says "track segments". A segment with no flagged update (only status updates, or only updates with no flag) is counted as "segments with no flagged update" and is in no class; the class "one flagged update" holds segments with exactly one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Position cross-check (with an ADS-B clip, read by the loader oa-encounter and oa-bench use): each tracked update with a flag, position and `mrtTime` is compared with every ADS-B aircraft interpolated linearly to `mrtTime` between the two reports around it (at most 5 s apart by default, 30 s at most; `--max-gap-s`; a segment faster than 600 m/s is left out and counted; ground reports are left out). A candidate is one aircraft inside the horizontal gate and, when both altitudes exist, the vertical gate (both inclusive; defaults 0.5, 1 and 2 NM with 500 ft, 1 NM primary). Per flag and gate the update is counted no candidate, exactly one, or ambiguous; only exactly-one is used. A horizontal-only count is kept at the primary gate. Updates with no position or time, with no flag, or on a pseudo, frozen or coasting track update are counted apart (a coasting position is dead-reckoned, not measured), as are updates whose `mrtTime` is outside the ADS-B clip's time span (OA-CEN-023). A gate above 10 NM, a gap above 30 s, or an unusable parameter is refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For exactly-one matches at the primary gate, per flag, the horizontal difference, the vertical difference, and the along-track and cross-track differences (STDDS minus ADS-B, along the ADS-B track, positive ahead and to the right; aircraft at 100 kt or more) are summarised by count, median, 10th, 90th and 99th percentile and a 20-bin histogram; the vertical differences of horizontal-only matches are summarised over a wide range to expose an altitude unit error. adsb=true is labelled ADS-B-fused and not independent of the truth (STARS fuses ADS-B into those updates, so its difference measures STARS latency and filtering, not accuracy). The adsb=false results are headlined by track class, and an adsb=false update on a mixed track is not ADS-B-free. Each matched cell prints the placebo-to-real match ratio, worded as a rough indication of unknown direction and not as an estimate of the chance share (OA-CEN-017). The ADS-B bracket width of the matches is counted (up to 2 s, 2 to 5, 5 to 10, over 10). A bias injected into synthetic STDDS updates shows in the matched distribution of adsb=false and not of adsb=true. adsb=true updates with a Mode S address are also checked by address, with no gate, and reported apart.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The along-track difference is also given as time (along-track metres over the ADS-B ground speed, aircraft at 100 kt or more); the ADS-B time is receipt time, so this is the STARS latency minus the ADS-B latency; a known clock offset in synthetic data is recovered, positive when the STDDS position is where the aircraft is later than the stated time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The cross-check counts and difference medians are split by track class and by facility, and absent without a clip.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The ADS-B reference is built with the gating of the tracker and the truth (`oa_truth::quality_check`, default config: source type adsb_icao, adsb_icao_nt or adsb_other, NACp, NIC, SIL, version, stale and range gates), in time order with per-aircraft carried state, not a parallel filter; reports on the ground are then dropped. The census prints the clip's reports by source type before any gating, what each gate removed, and what the time window left out. A TIS-B report on top of a radar-only update is not a candidate. `--from` and `--to` restrict both sides to a time of the UTC day (the ADS-B side padded by the interpolation gap and the placebo shift of 60 s, across midnight too); a window outside 0 to 86400 s, or a non-finite bound, is refused. The STDDS and ADS-B time spans are printed, and a run whose spans do not overlap (a wrong day or clip) exits 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The candidate search is exact at any latitude to 85 degrees and across the antimeridian: each segment is stored in every grid cell its bounding box touches after widening by the largest gate (in longitude at the box's highest latitude), longitude cells wrap, interpolation and the east difference take the short way round. Distances are in the tangent plane at the interpolated ADS-B point. Segments and updates above 85 degrees, and segments faster than 600 m/s, are counted and not used.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Coverage is counted apart from no candidate: per flag, the share of checked updates with any indexed ADS-B aircraft within 30 NM at their time.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The cross-check counts reconcile exactly with the update counts per flag: updates equal checked plus no position or time, above 85 degrees, no trackNum, pseudo, frozen or coasting update, outside the ADS-B clip's time span, and updates with the same time and position as the track's previous update (updates with the same key, time, position and flags are dropped earlier, OA-CEN-022); updates with no flag equal the not-checked no-flag count. The report also reconciles, with or without a clip, the input TAIS records read against the updates, the duplicates dropped, the updates outside the window and the updates with no time outside the window; with a clip, per flag and shift of the placebo, matched plus not matched plus outside the clip against checked. Each line says "reconciles" or "DOES NOT RECONCILE".

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A null control is run beside the real match: the same positions with the STDDS time shifted by plus and minus 60 s, printing per flag the outcome counts and the horizontal difference distribution of its exactly-one matches; the placebo exactly-one count (mean of the two shifts) over the real one is printed as a rough indication of unknown direction, not as an estimate of the chance share: the placebo shares route structure with the real match (aircraft in trail about 60 s apart, slow or circling aircraft matching themselves) and is not suppressed by the single-candidate rule the way a real chance match is. A placebo lookup at a window's edge finds its shifted ADS-B; a lookup whose shifted time lies outside the clip's time span (no window, or near the clip's edges) is counted as "placebo outside the clip", never as a non-match.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per flag the census prints the matches without a vertical difference, the distinct matched ADS-B aircraft and the distinct STDDS track segments with a match, and the distribution over track segments of each segment's median difference (segments with 3 or more matches). A segment is a run of one track number that a restart of the interval state (a gap over 120 s, an update flagged new, a resync) has not cut, so a recycled track number is not one aircraft; along and cross metres, like the time, leave out aircraft below 100 kt; a value is kept inside its histogram range after rounding to f32; the along-track-as-time figure leaves out aircraft below 100 kt; a class or facility cell with fewer than 30 matches prints "n<30" for a flag instead of medians; `--gate-nm` and `--gate-ft` without `--adsb` are refused; the histogram's upper edge is inclusive.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Track state is kept in step: a change of flag is counted only where an interval across it exists (so changes equal the changes by direction); a backwards update changes neither the time nor the flag of the track, an absent-flag update obeys the same backwards and reset rules, 3 backwards updates in a row restart the track (counted), and an update flagged new on a track number with state starts a new segment (counted).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Three checks against 4 GB. Each is an estimate under stated assumptions, not a guaranteed bound. (1) Before the ADS-B index is built: 16 bytes for every clip report, and for each report the padded window keeps, its point and an assumed 8 cell entries and 2 new grid cells (72 bytes each), all with 2x growth slack; a run past it is refused (exit 2) before the index is allocated. The cell assumption fails for a clip of faster or sparser aircraft or a larger gate. (2) After it: the index's own estimate. (3) While reading: what the census holds (interval lists, cross-check records, segments, with 2x Vec slack) and the copies that `finish` makes of each match, address match, placebo value and segment (three accumulators: all, class, facility), the tracks map, the segments and the set of seen update fingerprints. The quality-state map of the index build is counted, per distinct aircraft, in checks (1) and (2). Not counted: the loaded clip columns, the read buffers and the output. The report and the refusal message call the figure an estimate, not a bound. Updates left out by the time window are counted. A test sets the budget through `OA_STDDS_CENSUS_BUDGET_BYTES`, which exists for tests only.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Updates flagged pseudo, frozen or coasting (each read only when present and true) are never counted in the flag tallies, the track-segment class, the change counts or the interval census (the interval that starts at one is not counted either); they remain in the update totals and have their own counts per kind and flag, so the report shows how many coasts carried adsb=false and how many adsb=true. An all adsb=true segment with coasting adsb=false updates stays "all adsb=true". The identity shares (address, callsign, code 1200), the adsb=false share of flagged updates and the per-facility false share also leave out these updates, so they agree with the class lines; the update totals still count them.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An update with the same facility, `recSTARSSrcID`, `trackNum`, `mrtTime`, position and flags as one already seen, across files or within a file, is dropped before any count and counted as "duplicate updates dropped"; updates without a time or a track number are not checked for duplicates; the consecutive-repeat rule of the position check (OA-CEN-016) stays. With `--from` and `--to`, an update with no `mrtTime` is outside every window: it is excluded and counted as "no time, outside the window". `--from` and `--to` take whole seconds; a fractional value, or one whose milliseconds do not fit an i64, is a usage error (exit 2).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An update whose `mrtTime` lies outside the ADS-B clip's time span is counted, per flag, as "outside the ADS-B clip", never as no candidate or no ADS-B, and not checked; the run goes on. Exit 2 stays for no overlap at all. The spans are printed to the second.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This is a counts-only census/evaluation tool; it does not select operational tracks or warnings.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--surface-only` scans an immutable STDDS input snapshot without accumulating the TAIS census. It counts SMES Cat11 `asdexMsg/positionReport` rows only when the parsed message airport is exactly `KORD`, and reports their parser-UTC Unix-minute counts. Minute storage is bounded by a named 1,440-key one-day capacity; reports whose key cannot be retained, unreadable times, unreadable airport codes, whole-message refusals, damaged/unfinished frames, sealed drops, gzip damage/truncation, reader stalls and budget stops have named counters. Parser-kind and SMES field-error counts are explicitly all-facility. The report reconciles message frames seen with parse attempts and receive-time sealed frames and gives an explicit COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE verdict; COMPLETE requires nonempty input with no omitted, unassignable, untimed or refused input. Only the SMES Cat11 output is airport- and time-attributable; TAIS is a separate STARS product and Cat10 ASDE-X reports remain classification-only. This output is counts-only, guarded by OA-SEAL-001, and makes no inference that product absence or a capture gap establishes operational outage start or resumption.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The sealed hold-out data is listed once, in `crates/oa-sealed/sealed_paths.txt` (the data root, the entries `scds/rec-20261119/day2`, `day3`, `day4`, `runs*`, `scds/stdds-20261119-holdout*`, `scds/stdds-smoke-20261119*`, the days of OA-SEAL-010, and the windows of OA-SEAL-011); the Rust guard compiles the file in and the Python guard reads it, and both parse it to the same set. A list that does not parse refuses every path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A path is resolved before it is checked (relative paths, `..`, every link, a symlinked parent directory, a path not yet created through its nearest existing ancestor) and is refused, with a message that names the rule, if it is, is inside, resolves into or names (an entry's components in a row, as given or resolved) a sealed entry, if it is a directory that holds one, or if a link on it cannot be resolved. The shared guard owns the path rule only; keeping a sealed day's rows out of a file that also holds unsealed rows is a content rule that needs the tool's own parser (OA-SEAL-014). A file with more than one hard link is refused when it is opened, with a message that says why: a second name for sealed data under a neutral name passes the name check, and the real path of a descriptor is only one of its names (OA-SEAL-007). Consequences: `cp -al`, `rsync --link-dest` and hard-link dedup trees give files with a second name and are refused when opened, so such data is copied (`cp`, `rsync` without links) before it is read; a file whose metadata cannot be read is refused too (the check fails closed).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A tool that walks a directory checks every file it opens, through the guard's opener, not only its arguments.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Nothing switches the guard off: it reads no environment variable, flag or file, and an unknown option of the checker is a usage error.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every tool that reads recordings refuses a sealed input or output path with a nonzero exit, a message that names the rule, and nothing written: oa-compass, oa-encounter, oa-shadow, oa-track-run, oa-track-fusion, p002, oa-replay-diff, validate_candidate.py, comparison_reference.py, comparison_evaluator.py, run_comparison.py, track_set_score.py, replay_compare.sh, p002_build.sh, reproduce_zau.sh and zau_manifest.sh.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every bin and example target of the workspace, found from the manifests and the source layout, uses the sealed guard or is listed with a reason in `crates/oa-sealed/exempt_targets.txt`; a target with neither, a listed target that does not exist, and a listed target that uses the guard all fail the test. In the `src/` and `examples/` of every member crate (core crates included), a bare `File::open`, `File::open_buffered`, `File::options`, `OpenOptions`, `fs::read`, `fs::read_to_string`, `fs::read_dir`, `fs::metadata`, `fs::symlink_metadata`, `fs::copy`, `fs::hard_link` or `Command::new` fails the test unless `// seal-allow: <why>` with a reason is on the call's own line (trailing) or is the comment line before the next code line it covers. The generic spellings count: `<File>::open`, `<std::fs::File>::open` and a turbofish (`File::<T>::open`); an `include_bytes!` or `include_str!` whose argument is not a plain string literal (`env!`, `concat!`, a macro) is a bare read; and a `pub use` of anything in `std::fs` or `std::process` is one too (it re-exports the functions to the rest of the crate). A manifest that gains `libc`, `memmap`, `memmap2` or `walkdir` needs a `# seal-note: <why>` comment on its line or the line before, or a test fails. A name counts when it is used at all, so a function passed as a value (`.map(fs::read_to_string)`, `File::open` as a value) is a use, and so is the `.read_dir()` method. The scan reads each file with a lexer that tells plain, raw and byte strings, characters, lifetimes, line comments and nested block comments apart, with string state carried over lines; imports are read as use trees (`use std::fs::*`, grouped `use std::{fs::{self, File as F}, ..}`, `as` aliases of functions, types and the modules `std::fs` and `std::process`), and `type X = File;` (also `OpenOptions` and `Command`, through a path or generics) makes `X` a bare type. Under `src/`, only a module declared `#[cfg(test)] mod` is skipped (an inline one with its body, a file module `mod name;` with the file and every module it declares); no file is skipped by its name, and any other `#[cfg(test)]` item is scanned. An allow with no bare call on the line it covers is stale and fails, and an allow inside a skipped test module is not counted; the number of allows is pinned exactly in the test (`ALLOW_COUNT`, now 152), not a budget. `tests/`, `benches/` and `build.rs` of every crate are scanned the same way when the file names the real data root (a string that holds `OPENATCA_`, which covers `OPENATCA_RAW`, `OPENATCA_DATA`, `OPENATCA_SCDS`, `OPENATCA_ADSB_CLIP`, `OPENATCA_SNAPSHOT`, `OPENATCA_REC`, `OPENATCA_SENSORSIM_CLIP`, `OPENATCA_NASR`, `OPENATCA_CIFP` and any other, or `openatca-data`; a comment or an identifier such as a constant does not count), and a `#[cfg(test)]` module, inline or a file, that names it is scanned too instead of skipped: there a bare call needs the same allow (a temp dir, a fixture, a built binary), and a read of the data goes through `oa_sealed`; a file that does not name the root reads fixtures and temp dirs bare. Stated exceptions, with the reason: oa-arinc424 (a no-dependency crate, so it cannot use oa-sealed), oa-geo (a core crate, which does not depend on the shell crate oa-sealed) and oa-trace (walks the repository's own sources and registers, no data). The bare opens of the first two are in tests only (fixtures and the env-named `OPENATCA_CIFP` and `OPENATCA_GEODTEST` inputs); a test pins the count of bare calls per file, found by the same scan with nothing skipped, and fails if either crate gains one. `oa-mva`'s `pdftotext` runs on a path the guard has checked as given and as resolved. Not covered: a test module that is declared `#[cfg(test)] mod` in a source file is not scanned even when it names the data root, and a file module is matched to its declaration by the usual module paths without reading `#[path]`.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The list holds `window <from-UTC> <to-UTC>` lines (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, half-open, from before to): every row or frame whose time falls in one is sealed whichever file holds it. `oa_sealed::in_sealed_window(unix_ns)` and `sealed_windows()` expose them, `sealed_guard.in_sealed_window` and `Guard.windows` do the same in Python, and both parsers read the lines to the same set and refuse a malformed or empty window. The list has `window 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z 2026-11-23T00:17:00Z` (the three ADS-B days and hold-out days A to C of the four-day recording). Both parsers widen every listed window by 15 minutes on each side when they read it (`oa_sealed::WINDOW_MARGIN_NS`, `sealed_guard.WINDOW_MARGIN_NS`; the listed text is kept), so the span the gates and `DropWindow::sealed()` use is 2026-11-19T23:45:00Z to 2026-11-23T00:32:00Z. The margin covers the rounding of a fraction, differences between a scan and a parser, and the lag between a feed's own time and the receive time of its frame (the SFDPS lag floor is 58 s): development data within 15 minutes of either edge is dropped and counted. A list with no window line seals every instant (`Sealed::in_window`, `Guard.in_window`), and a tool prints `seal list has no window: every timed row is dropped` on standard error at start (`DropReport`, `sealed_guard.production`), still failing closed; a list that does not parse prints `seal list does not parse: every timed row is dropped and every sealed path refused` the same way (`oa_sealed::start_warning`, `sealed_guard.start_warning`). Several windows are read to one span, the hull from the earliest start to the latest end, with any gap between them inside it (`Sealed::drop_window`, `sealed_window_ms`; the gates `in_window` test each window).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A test or tool that walks a directory uses `oa_sealed::walk_unsealed` (Python `Guard.walk_unsealed`): a directory or file the guard refuses is skipped and counted, never descended into or opened, a directory that only holds a sealed entry (the data root, `raw/adsblol`) is walked, and a sealed walk root is an error. `oa_sealed::read` and `read_to_string` read through the guard's opener. `fuzz/make_corpora.py` reads and globs through the guard. The walk visits each canonical directory once: the entries of a directory are sorted bytewise before any is walked, so of two names of one directory (a sibling link such as `a/x -> ../real` beside `real`) the first in that order is the one walked; a repeat visit, and a link back, is counted as `already_visited` (`Walk::already_visited`; the Python guard returns it as the third item), apart from the sealed entries counted in `skipped`. Nesting deeper than 64 and a root that does not exist are errors, not a silent stop or an empty walk; the files are sorted bytewise by the string form of the path, the same in both guards. Tests: a self-link, two self-links, a sibling link, a deep tree, a missing root and the sort order (Rust and Python).
