non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every library function that takes a path and opens it for reading opens it through the guard: `oa_zip::read_archive_file`, `oa_nasr::open`, `oa_dof::read_file`, `oa_tiff::read_file` and the `oa-replay-diff` file readers; a sealed path is an I/O error that names OA-SEAL-001.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The readers drop every row or frame whose time falls in a sealed window (OA-SEAL-011) and count it: `oa_bench::input::load_adsb` (a frame with a row in the window is dropped whole and its rows counted; `AdsbClip::sealed_window_dropped`) and `for_each_adsb_frame` (a frame with a row in the window is not passed on), `oa_truth::clip::read_clip` (`read_clip_counted`; a frame with a row in the window is dropped whole, and is in no other count, `oa_adsb::reports_extend_unsealed`), the `oa-replay` recording reader (frames by receive time; `MergeReport::sealed_window_dropped`) and the `oa-stdds-census` recording reader (`ReadStats`). A row at the `from` instant of the widened window (the listed start less 15 minutes) and one at the last nanosecond before its `to` (the listed end plus 15 minutes) are dropped; one at `from - 1 ns` and one at `to` are kept. Every tool built on them prints `sealed-window rows dropped: N` (also when N is 0) and, where it writes a report or README, records the line there: oa-bench (report note), oa-compass (README), oa-encounter (summary), oa-shadow (report header), oa-stdds-census (the read section); oa-truth-check, oa-sensorsim, oa-track and its examples, oa-replay print it. The message loaders do the same by frame and by record: `oa_bench::input::load_with` (SFDPS, TBFM, TFMS; frames by receive time, and a document with a message whose own time is in the window even when its frame was received outside it (the keys of the list below, which the decoders read; the loader has no key list of its own); `Loaded::sealed_window_dropped`, `Counts::sealed_window_dropped`), the `oa-replay` pipeline (documents by the times of their messages, and an ADS-B frame by its rows, each dropped whole; `Pipeline::sealed_window_dropped`), `oa-feed replay` (frames; `Report::sealed_window_dropped`), the `oa-stdds-census` reader (TAIS records by `mrtTime`) and the `stdds_summary` example. For these the printed count is frames plus records and the tool says so. The same holds for `oa-flight` (`oa-flight-sfdps`: frames by receive time from the merge, rows by their own time; a run stopped early by `--to` does not count the frames dropped before the stop), the SFDPS join of `oa-encounter` (added to the clip's count), the recordings and clip of `oa-stdds-ref` (frames by receive time, TAIS records by `mrtTime`), and for `oa-scope-replay` (clip frames by receive time, and a frame with a row in the window dropped whole and in no decode counter, through `oa_adsb::reports_extend_unsealed` on a per-frame scratch), the `oa-replay` pipeline's ADS-B frames (whole frame, by any row's time; the frame is in no error, frame, message, byte or `fed` count) and FNS rows (issue or cancel time; the validity span is not a message time), the `oa-adsb` archive reader (trace rows; `Stats::sealed_window_dropped`, and `oa-adsb-clip` refuses, OA-SEAL-015), `oa-wind-check adsb` and the `stdds_summary` example, which drops inside the decoder. The window is a required argument of every decoder, so a caller cannot forget it: `oa_stdds::Limits`, `oa_fixm::Limits` and `oa_notam::Limits` have no `Default` and a constructor `Limits::new(DropWindow)`; `oa_tbfm::new_rows` and `oa_tfms::new_rows` take it as their last argument. `oa_sealed::DropWindow` is the half-open span in Unix ms; `DropWindow::sealed()` is the sealed window (`oa_sealed::sealed_window_ms()`) and is what every tool passes; `DropWindow::empty_for_tests_and_fuzz()` drops nothing and is for tests and fuzz targets only (its name says so). A test per shell asserts the window it passes equals the sealed one (oa-replay `doc_fixm_limits`, `doc_notam_limits` and the TBFM and TFMS row tables, which `oa-bench` and `oa-flight` use through `Reader::drop_windows` and `decoder_limits`, the census, the `oa-stdds-ref` loader and the `stdds_summary` example). A document is dropped whole by the times of its messages. Every decoder's first step is a pre-scan of the whole document (the whole message for stdds), before any counter, row, table or string store is touched. It reads each message's or record's own time by the feed's known path, directly from the parsed tree, in any attribute order: its own times by the feed's known path (the key list below). If any is in the window the whole document is dropped and a sealed outcome carries only the count of its messages (or records): `Stats::sealed_window_dropped` or `Outcome::sealed_dropped`. It is in no other count (no message, document, row, kind, rejection, refused-field, field-error, shape, flag, unknown-path or unknown-root count) and touches no table or string store. No refusal can be caused by an in-window message, because the pre-scan has no record or row limit and runs before the decode. There is no window rollback in any decoder. Every pre-scan reads each value with the decoder's own value reader and parser (the same function, not a copy; the fixm survey calls `oa_fixm::prescan`), so the scan and the decoder cannot differ in what they read. TFMS TMI-list counts are therefore for the whole document, not per entry. The rule for what is a window key: every observation time and every actual-event time the decoder parses into a row or a statistic is a key (a message stamped after the window can report an event inside it); a reference time (an estimate, a schedule or a validity time such as ETA, ETD, STA, effective, begin, end, original and filed times) is not. The keys per feed, exactly as the code reads them: TAIS `track/mrtTime` and `recSAFAReceiptTime` of each `record` (`recSTARSTimestamp` is a time of day, not a time); ASDE-X `time` of each report; SFDPS (fixm) the `timestamp` and `positionTime` attributes of any element, and the `time` attribute of an `actual` element (the actual departure); TBFM the `msgTime` attribute, the envelope time of an `env` (`envTime`) or `mis` (`misTime`) document, and `ctm`; TFMS the attributes `sourceTimeStamp`, `airlineOutTime`, `airlineOffTime`, `airlineOnTime`, `airlineInTime`, `runwayDeparture`, `runwayArrival`, `gateDeparture`, `gateArrival`, `boundaryCrossingTime`, `lastUpdateTime` and `flightCreation`, the `timeValue` of an `etd` with `etdType` ACTUAL or an `eta` with `etaType` ACTUAL, and the element text of `timeAtPosition`, of any element named `time` (an oceanic position's), of `eventTime`, `dateSent` and `lastUpdate` (flow and TMI messages), of `timeOfDeparture` and `timeOfArrival` unless `estimated="true"`, and of `coordinationTime` and `newCoordinationTime` with `type` ACTUAL; NOTAM the text of `issued` and `canceled`. Borderline times, keyed because when unsure a time is keyed (a false drop costs a document of development data; a missed key leaks hold-out data): the TFMS `flightCreation` (when the flight was created in the system, which is the time of the message that created it) and the TBFM `ctm` (a crossing time, which can be an actual one). Not keys, as reference times: ETA, ETD and STA of any other type, `igtd`, the original departure and arrival, the arrival and departure fix times, the `startTime`, `stopTime` and `endTime` of a restriction or advisory, the TBFM schedule and estimate times, and the validity times of a NOTAM. A scan reads a value with the decoder's own reader, so it reads what the decoder reads: character references are decoded and whitespace is trimmed where the decoder trims; text that a comment or CDATA section splits is one value for STDDS and TFMS and is a bad field, not a time, for NOTAM. A repeated element of a key name is read too. The STDDS scan skips a record outside the message's namespace, as the decoder does; the other scans read an element of a key name in any namespace (so such a document is dropped too: the closed failure). A time that cannot be read falls to the receive-time gate of its frame; a document refused whole (not XML, wrong root) has no known time and is counted as refused. Development-day documents near the window edges that carry an in-window message are lost whole, and counted. `DropWindow::sealed()` fails closed: if the sealed list has no window or does not parse it is a window covering all time (`DropWindow::all_time()`); `oa_sealed::sealed_window_ms()` is its span and `Sealed::in_window` (so `in_sealed_window`, the frame and row gates) seals all time for a list with no window line, so the gates and the decoders agree. The millisecond span rounds the start down and the end up, so a window that is not a whole number of milliseconds leaves no gap. The `oa-bench` scan (hints, addresses, handoffs, routes) runs only on documents that passed the pre-scan, and `docs` counts a document after it. The replay pipeline counts a frame and a message only after the decode, and only for a document that was not dropped (`Pipeline::last_doc_dropped`); the byte count of `oa-replay` leaves out the bytes of such a frame, as it does for a frame dropped by receive time. An ADS-B frame with any row in the window is dropped whole in the same way (its rows are counted as dropped; it is in no frame, message, byte or `fed` count). The replay clock and the sweeps use frame receive times, which the gate has checked are outside the widened window; the clock moves for the frame of a dropped document too, and what it prints (the replay time and its own counters) comes from those receive times, not from the document. `oa-feed` health and the `oa-bench` input digests count by receive time and are file identities, covered by the 15-minute margin. The `oa-flight-sfdps` merge report's bytes are not printed. The input digests and byte totals of `oa-bench` are file identities, like the SHA-256 that `oa-stdds-ref` prints, and not statistics. A recording's byte count (`oa-replay`, `oa-feed replay`) is the bytes after the window gate: the bytes of a frame dropped by receive time are not in it. A failed read still adds what was counted so far (`oa-stdds-ref` `load_file_counted`, `stdds_summary`, the fixm survey, which uses `DropWindow::sealed()`, drops a file with a message in the window whole before any count (`files` counts the kept files only; the dropped ones are in the drop line), and returns an error through `main` instead of unwrapping). The SHA-256 `oa-stdds-ref` prints is a file identity (of the file as a whole, as a name for it), not a statistic of its contents. `oa-bench` and `oa-stdds-census` record the line in their report and also print one stderr line at exit, which is the same count printed once. Other message kinds (service status, classified only) carry no row time and go by the receive time of their frame. Tests assert the `records:`, a TAIS field and a flag count, a refused message whose early records are in the window, the fixm, TBFM, TFMS and NOTAM stats, the oa-replay TFMS flow rows, and the oa-bench tables. `oa-scope-replay` prints its line on every exit, an empty window included, and its decoder `records` and `kept` counts are after the window filter. A row or record with no time of its own is kept, backstopped by the receive time of its frame where the reader has one: SFDPS rows without a timestamp, TBFM/TFMS rows without a message time, a TAIS record without `mrtTime`, a raw `.msg` file (no frame header, so nothing to count by receive time). `oa-compass slice` reads the `.ast` files of an export, which carry only a time of day, and relies on the export, which never writes sealed rows; the Python result tools (`run_comparison.py`, `track_set_score.py` and the like) read derived results, not data. The printed line is printed once per run, by an `oa_sealed::DropReport` that the tool makes at the top of its run and adds each reader's count to as the reader returns; the line is printed when the report is dropped, so every exit that comes back through `main` prints it: a `?` error, `--hours`, a stop at `--to` (which adds the merge's own count of frames dropped before the stop), a refusal and a failed read. No tool calls `process::exit` after reading has started. The count is the sum of the per-reader counts (`Loaded`, `MergeReport`, clip counts), each input counted once (an input read twice is not counted twice); the process-wide counter (`oa_sealed::window_dropped_total`) is kept only as a test cross-check. A test asserts the line for each tool that has an integration test.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This protects source-data and holdout boundaries; it is an engineering data-control requirement, not an aviation decision function.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `oa-adsb-clip` creates the sidecar and then the clip, each with `create_new` (`O_EXCL`), so nothing is replaced, truncated or followed (a dangling link included) and no second name for an existing file appears; an existing output or `.source` is refused, and a failure removes the files this run created and only those, and refuses to clip a report whose time is in a sealed window: exit 2, nothing written, the count printed as `sealed-window rows dropped: N` (the reports are counted, not clipped). Otherwise it writes `<out>.source` next to the clip (not for `--out -`): each input path with its SHA-256, the window (`--from`, `--to` in Unix nanoseconds, `none` when open) and the counts (rows seen, outside the box, outside the window, kept, frames, sealed-window rows dropped). A test makes the clip name appear between the pre-check and the create (a hook that exists only in test builds) and fails if the create is `File::create` again; another checks the cleanup of a write failure.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A STDDS record is paired with the tracker and the ADS-B truth by its Mode S address (`acAddress`, 24 bits) only; a record without an address is counted and never paired.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every STDDS record has a class from its own flags, by one function, read as the census reads them and only when a flag's bit is in `present` (an absent flag is never false): `track/pseudo`, `track/frozen` or `track/coast` present and true is "pseudo, frozen or coasting"; otherwise `track/adsb` present gives "adsb=false" or "adsb=true", and absent gives "adsb absent". The names state the flag value, not a meaning: what `track/adsb` means is not confirmed (the census measures it).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every metric, count and time-offset distribution is reported per class; no line or section blends the classes, "pseudo, frozen or coasting" is never pooled with another, and a class's records are fitted as tracks of their own.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per class, three error sets are computed on the same paired samples: tracker minus STDDS, ADS-B truth minus STDDS, tracker minus ADS-B truth (the second is the diagnostic for STDDS following ADS-B).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per STDDS track the stamp offset is fitted against the ADS-B truth only, never the tracker, over -15 s to +15 s in 0.1 s steps minimising along-track error, ties toward zero; every metric is reported at offset 0 and at the fitted offset, and a track with no fit has no fitted samples.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The offset search is exact at its edges, flags an offset at either end of the range, and refuses a fit with fewer than 8 samples that have a moving truth at every offset (OA-SRF-015 gives the reason).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Tracker fixes are interpolated between rows at most 5 s apart; at a track end a fix is extrapolated by the end row's velocity up to 1 s and counted, and refused beyond that.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per set: horizontal error, along and cross track, altitude difference (feet) and velocity difference (m/s), each with n, rms, mean, p50, p95 and p99; an absent value is no data, never 0.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The summary carries the SHA-256 of each input file and one digest over the summary and the per-sample CSV; the CSV (record place, class, status, offset and errors) carries neither. Both outputs are byte-identical for the same inputs given by the same paths.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool uses the shared guard (`oa-sealed`, OA-SEAL-001, OA-SEAL-002) and no guard of its own: every path it is given (the STDDS files, the ADS-B clip, the output folder) is checked before anything is read or created, and a sealed one (a sealed folder, a sealed ADS-B day, a link into sealed data) exits 2 with a message that names the path.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every file the tool reads is opened by check, open and verify-the-open through the shared guard, so a link swapped between the check and the open is refused (exit 2, the path named). The tool walks no directory.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The text and the per-sample CSV hold counts and aggregate statistics only: never a track number, callsign, Mode S address, time or position of a record.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A `.oaf` or `.oaf.gz` recording is read into records with counts of frames, other products and damage, and the SHA-256 of the file's stored bytes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A record with no time or no position is counted as its own unpaired reason, never paired.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Tracks that are not fitted are reported per class by reason: no ADS-B truth over the +-15 s window at enough samples (the track has at least 8 sample records), and fewer than 8 usable samples (too few records, or a covered truth too slow to give a direction).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool creates `stdds_ref.txt` and `stdds_ref.csv` with create-new and never overwrites: an existing output (or link) exits 1 with its path named, before any work; each output path is checked through the shared guard before it is created, and one that leads into sealed data exits 2.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report states the assumed units (STDDS altitude feet, velocity m/s east and north) and which tracker altitude is compared, and prints per class the median STDDS altitude against the median truth altitude and the median ratio of STDDS speed to truth speed on the paired samples, with "units suspect" when the altitude medians (floored at 100 ft) differ by more than a factor of 10 or the speed ratio is outside 0.8 to 1.25.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Offset calibration requires a positive address and complete source-facility/track key. Ambiguous duplicate timestamps are excluded without choosing class order; every unambiguous class transition and declared reuse gap starts a separate fit segment, including A-to-B-to-A.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Comparison input, retained records, fit work and output bytes have checked limits. Reports distinguish each mode's cohort from the same-record raw/fitted intersection and publish per-metric denominators. In-sample calibration and unverified units remain explicit limitations.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Summary, CSV and JSON are published without replacing existing outputs; a final content/provenance marker binds all three. Cooperating same-host writers hold one publisher lock. This does not establish distributed fencing or automatic recovery of a partial report set.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates recorded tracks against reference data and does not feed scores into operational tracking.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Published-time cohort selection uses explicit half-open bounds before offset fitting, retains the complete ADS-B boundary context, and counts selected, untimed and outside rows against the post-seal denominator. Oversized retained sets are refused before selection mutates any row.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The time an aircraft reached a point is the time of closest approach of its ADS-B truth path to the point, interpolated linearly between the two samples either side of it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A crossing counts only when the closest approach is within the configured cut distance (development value 2 NM); the closest approach of every (flight, point) searched is counted by distance bucket in the report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A passage is at an edge, and not scored (counted as such), only when the segment of its closest approach, or a segment directly next to it, begins or ends at the start or end of the truth path or at a hole in the truth; a path with no sample is counted separately.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An estimate is scored against one passage of the bound leg, chosen by the rule of OA-LTJ-049 from the passages whose closest approach is not before the time the estimate was issued. When every passage is before it, the last one is taken: the event happened before the message, and the error is kept. The estimated time never chooses the passage.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The touchdown time is the middle of the gap between the last airborne report and the first ground report, the gap at most the configured limit (development value 30 s); the last airborne report is within the runway radius (5 NM) of the airport reference point; a landing outside either is counted by reason.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The bin of an estimate is that of its stated lead, the estimate minus the issue time of the message that carried it; the bins are 0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20-40, 40-60 and 60-120 minutes, lower edge included; a stated lead that is negative or outside them is excluded and counted. The actual time minus the issue time is a sensitivity binning.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The error is the estimate minus the actual time, in seconds: positive when the estimate is later than what happened.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each bin reports n, the median, 95th and 99th percentile of the absolute error (nearest rank, OA-LTJ-025) as the headline columns, the signed median and mean as bias, the signed 5th and 95th percentile as spread, and the RMS and the share over 1,800 s, computed in a fixed order whatever order the values arrive in; the 95th and 99th percentiles and the spread percentiles are printed only for n of 100 or more, else `n<100` (empty in the CSV).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight that carries an aircraft address joins by it when a truth leg of that address overlaps the flight's interval; otherwise it has no truth, and its callsign is not tried.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight without an address joins by callsign when the truth legs with that callsign that overlap its interval are of one aircraft; several aircraft is ambiguous, none is no truth.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A flight with no address and no callsign, and a flight whose records name more than one address, each have their own join outcome.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every flight is counted under one join outcome and every estimate is either in a bin or under one exclusion reason; a flight with no truth is counted and its estimates are excluded, none is dropped; a callsign join that fails the conditions of OA-LTJ-030 counts as no truth.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report text and the CSV are a function of the counts alone, and every number carries its n.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: ERAM's predicted time at each point of a converted route is scored against the crossing of the point, by look-ahead from the route message; a point's position is its own coordinates, else the one place its name has in the recordings.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TBFM's meter-fix and scheduled times are scored against the crossing of the meter fix, and its runway times against the landing at the arrival airport.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: TFMS's arrival estimates are scored against the landing at the arrival airport; its departure estimates are counted and not scored.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool takes the three recording directories, one or more ADS-B clips and the output directory, and refuses a missing, repeated or unknown argument. A NASR archive and a places file are optional. Its usage text prints every default and every fixed setting, and the test checks that text against the values the tool uses.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Output files are written under a temporary name and renamed only after all are written. On any failure every temporary file is removed, and the error names the files already renamed, which keep their new content; a failed run can therefore leave new and old files side by side, and says so.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The tool refuses every input and output path that resolves into sealed data, before anything is opened or created.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An airport's place is taken from NASR (`APT_BASE`, by its FAA identifier and its ICAO identifier) or the places file, never derived from the recordings; an airport with no place is excluded and counted as airport unknown.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A named point's place is its own coordinates in a route message, else NASR (`FIX_BASE`, `NAV_BASE`, and an airport where a route names one) as overridden by the places file; a name with no place is unknown and counted as an exclusion; a malformed places line is refused naming its line.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A name with several places takes the one nearest the flight's route and the estimate is counted as ambiguous-resolved: for ERAM, the distance by great circle from the candidate to the nearest of the filed route's neighbouring points with coordinates (two each side in the same route), else of the flight's other route points with coordinates, else of the flown path (thinned to at most 200 places), and the report counts which was used; for TBFM the flown path; the name is refused and counted as ambiguous when its places are more than 500 NM apart or the flight has no reference place.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Scored rows are in four blocks: address-joined and airborne at issue (the headline), address-joined and not airborne at issue (pre-departure, labelled as including departure delay), and the same two for callsign joins; each block reports as OA-LTJ-008, with the rows kept whose event was before the issue counted per bin. Headline-only diagnostics: the error by actual lead, a histogram, the error against the TFMS actual arrival time, the touchdown at the last airborne and at the first ground report, the gap of the landings used, one row per flight and bin (the last message in the bin) for every kind, and the crossing at the cuts 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 NM.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `--nasr` reads `FIX_BASE`, `NAV_BASE` and `APT_BASE` from a NASR CSV archive through the sealed-data guard; the report gives, for ERAM name-only route points, TBFM meter-fix and scheduling-fix names and TFMS arrival codes, how many names and occurrences are not found, have one place, have several within 500 NM, or several over 500 NM, and lists the 20 most frequent names not resolvable.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Percentiles are nearest rank, as `oa-bench` and `p002` define them: the value at 1-based rank ceil(p n / 100) of the sorted values, no interpolation.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A passage in progress at the issue time is chosen by its closest approach like any other; one whose closest approach is before the issue is the last passage and is kept.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A change from airborne to ground is a landing only when no airborne report follows within 30 s of the last airborne report and that report is below the airport elevation (NASR) plus 1,000 ft or below 80 m/s; refused changes near the airport are counted (touch and go, blip, too high and fast); a landing elsewhere is a diversion exclusion; a leg with no ground report is excluded as `bound leg has no ground report`, checked after the look-ahead range; the landing exclusions are split by whether the bound leg ends inside the clip box or within 10 NM of its edge.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A row whose event happened before the issue time and whose estimate is not before it is scored, not excluded, and counted per bin.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Each message binds exactly one truth leg of the flight's own. A leg in progress at the issue time binds only when the aircraft is airborne on it (OA-LTJ-031), it lands after the issue, and it took off within 10 NM of the departure airport or lands within 10 NM of the arrival airport, or, with neither airport known, carries the flight's callsign; a leg that had landed before the issue never binds as in progress. Otherwise the first leg not yet airborne at the issue binds when it starts within 3 h after the issue and took off at the departure airport, or, with the departure airport unknown or not in NASR, carries the flight's callsign; else none (counted as no leg, no leg of the flight's own, or departure past the window). The crossing and the landing are searched only on that leg; joined flights whose interval touched more than one leg are counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A callsign join needs a leg that starts no later than 3 h after the flight's first issue (or is in progress at it) and, when the departure or arrival airport is known, that took off at the departure airport or landed at the arrival airport (within 10 NM of its place); a join refused is counted by the condition that refused it.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A row is airborne at issue when the issue time is between the bound leg's first airborne report and its landing (the first ground report of the first change to ground that holds up, OA-LTJ-027), or its last report when it does not land; otherwise it is pre-departure.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report header gives, for each system, the flights in the recording, the flights joined to an ADS-B aircraft in the clip and their share, the flights with a scored estimate, and the estimates excluded because the bound leg has no ground report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The NASR archive and the places file go through the sealed-data guard, by the tool's path check and by the readers themselves.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: No two distinct NASR airports share an airport key; a shared key is detected and counted in the report header.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An in-progress leg that is another flight's is refused and counted, and the message falls through to the flight's own next leg: a turnaround where one fix lies on both the inbound and the outbound legs scores the outbound flight's message against the outbound passage only.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A leg that landed before the issue time (taxi-in) never binds as in progress; it is counted as refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The airborne span of a leg runs from its first airborne report to the first ground report of the first change to ground that holds up, else to its last report; a leg with no airborne report has none.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The landing persistence of 30 s is measured from the last airborne report.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A passage is at an edge only as OA-LTJ-003 says: a path that merely begins or ends within the cut, far from the closest approach, is not.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For each kind and stated-lead bin the report gives the estimates offered, those with no leg (of which no leg of the flight's own, and departure past the window) and those scored; the landing exclusions are split by where the bound leg ends (OA-LTJ-027); a table gives, per arrival airport (the 30 with most estimates), the estimates offered, scored and the share.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For every kind the report gives the headline as one message per flight and stated-lead bin (the last message of the flight in the bin, all its rows), beside the message-weighted one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A leg ends at the clip box edge when its last place is within 10 NM of an edge of the box.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The estimate of a name with several places in an ERAM route is resolved against the route's neighbouring points, else the route's other points, else the flown path, and the report counts each.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A runway or arrival estimate whose stated lead is out of range is excluded for that reason before the ground-report check.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The headline crossing is searched at the cuts 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 NM, the headline stays at 2 NM, every row scored at a smaller cut is scored at each larger one (OA-LTJ-048; a violation is counted), and headline crossings whose closest approach is from 2 to 5 NM are reported apart as the abeam table; every cut reports its rows per bin.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The TBFM `sta_sfx` and `sta_rwy` kinds are labelled a schedule target (metering), not a forecast.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The passage of a (message, point) is chosen once, among the passages found at the largest cut, by the rule of OA-LTJ-049; each cut scores that passage when its closest approach is within the cut and it is not at an edge, so a row scored at a cut is scored at every larger one.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The report gives, for the ERAM headline rows at 60 to 120 minutes under the binding of the earlier rounds (in progress or next leg with no ownership test), what became of each under the present binding, counted by reason.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A run of consecutive truth segments within the cut is split into passages where the distance to the point rises 0.5 NM above the run's closest approach and then falls 0.5 NM below its largest, so each loop of a hold is its own passage. Of the passages not before the issue the first whose closest approach is within 0.5 NM is chosen; if none, the closest (the earliest on a tie); if none is at or after the issue, the last before it. The report counts the (message, point) rows with more than one passage and those whose choice differs from the runs-not-split closest rule.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Next to each headline the report gives, per bin, the share of the offered rows excluded as truth path never within the cut, passage at an edge, and no ground report, and the headline recomputed without the rows whose place was resolved against the flown path. Exact duplicate rows (same flight, point, issue time and estimate) are dropped before scoring and counted.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An in-progress leg is owned by a flight whose departure and arrival airports are both known only when the departure matches (or the leg begins at the clip box edge) and the arrival matches (or the leg ends there), at least one of them matching; the rows whose bound leg this changes are counted. ADS-B legs carry no flight-plan identity, so no binding by GUFI is possible.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A truth path segment longer than 30 s is a hole for the edge rule and is counted (the truth answers only within 10 s of a report on both sides, so none arises at a step of 30 s or less).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The opt-in ORD arrival experiment uses the route and flight identity recorded at receipt, the latest eligible airborne ADS-B report at or before that issue, and the latest available TBFM estimate at the same cutoff. Ambiguous observations are excluded and counted. The report is aggregate and states its offered, issued and scored denominators.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An issued arrival forecast provides 5, 10 and 20 minute positions and a selected-fix ETA when inputs support them. Scoring uses future truth without bridging gaps, the first valid post-issue meter passage, and optional comparisons available at issue time. A missing measurement remains absent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The arrival forecast uses an assigned altitude only from a supported simple SFDPS assignment received by the issue cutoff. Selection is by source event time among available updates. Malformed assignments, valid non-simple replacements, conflicts at the same source stamp, uncertain availability that could change the selection, and incomplete bounded history withhold the scalar with a named reason. The report counts assignment states per issued forecast.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The opt-in arrival raw-rate diagnostic counts evidence over the frozen issue cohort using unique, compatible preceding barometric observations of the same ADS-B source class. It considers up to 128 prior rows and uses observations within 10 seconds to compare displacement against its illustrative 50-foot tolerance. It uses existing issues and forecasts.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Arrival prediction and truth interpolation follow the shorter longitude displacement across the antimeridian. Closest-approach segments also follow the shorter displacement across the planar chart boundary opposite the scoring point.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: At a positive issue cutoff, the route selector forecasts the latest received revision for the specified full flight GUFI, independently of candidate order. A selected amendment changes the supplied route geometry and its resulting meter ETA.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Other-GUFI and post-cutoff revisions do not participate in route selection. The forecast envelope and shell report retain the selected plan ID, full GUFI, receive time and issue cutoff; future evidence does not alter that issue.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Available revisions at an equal receive timestamp with differing plan identity or route geometry are refused. Identical duplicates are deterministic in the core selector.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Missing/blank plan identity, missing flight identity, nonpositive receive or cutoff time, more than 256 selector candidates, or more than 256 fixes in an eligible route is refused before unbounded route processing. Only the bounded selected geometry is copied for prediction.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The shell considers every captured revision of an admitted flight at its issue cutoff. A latest amendment removing the selected meter or changing the destination out of the admitted ORD flow cannot disappear in favor of an older route; that issue is refused.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Shell cutoff selection preserves the selected revision's geometry and provenance together and ignores later revisions. The experiment retains its first-eligible issue per flight; it does not update that frozen issue for later in-flight amendments.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The shell checks raw route spans against the 256-fix limit before route-point resolution or allocation in flow admission and cutoff revision construction.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Malformed and over-limit route rows are counted and skipped as issue candidates, while retained in the full flight's revision history. A future-only bad revision cannot veto an earlier issue; a bad revision available at an attempted cutoff refuses that issue.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Same-receive-time, same-plan, identical-geometry revisions carrying conflicting selected-fix ERAM estimate payloads are refused in either input order. No estimate is favored or used to select forecast geometry.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per-flight histories are sorted once within the 500,000 captured-route limit. Each issue uses a binary-searched cutoff prefix and refuses more than 256 available revisions before examining geometry. Across candidate attempts, revision examinations are bounded by the captured-row limit times the revision limit; each examined raw span is bounded at 256 fixes.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Operational source-ordered route selection is bounded to 256 revisions and 256 route fixes per cutoff, is independent of candidate input order, and never lets a later-received older source event roll back a newer source event already available.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Within the 256-candidate budget, revisions received after the issue cutoff cannot affect selection or cause refusal for malformed revision payload or geometry. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Contradictory eligible route payloads for the same full GUFI, reporting centre and source timestamp are explicitly refused independent of input order. Distinct reporting centres are independent.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Equivalent same-source route payload duplicates are harmless. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The latest eligible source revision is never silently replaced by an older revision when its route is empty, invalid or over the route-fix bound. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Every source-ordered route selection, successful or refused, retains its offered denominator. Other-flight, other-centre, future, eligible and unexamined counts partition all input candidates; selected, older-source, restated and withheld counts partition eligible candidates. non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This measures recorded landing-time estimates against truth; it does not provide an operational ETA or command.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The offline evaluator compares independently supplied same-address hazard windows with a caller-declared complete alert log. Each accepted encounter has exactly one timely, late or missed warning-onset outcome, and these counts sum to the encounter denominator. This is a synthetic development measure, not operational qualification.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A warning onset inside the window at its deadline is timely; after the deadline through the inclusive end is late. A compressed episode with a first warning before the window and an end inside or after it does not prove continuing warning: the evaluator refuses an ambiguous outcome unless an independent in-window onset already establishes timely credit. Neither the episode end nor a loss observation extends warning evidence.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Nuisance records are supplied alert records whose inclusive alert interval overlaps no full-address hazard window; the alert record count is reported as their denominator.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Terminal lost-altitude records and records with a recorded loss observation inside a same-address hazard window are counted separately. A compressed record's `protect_ns` is a point observation; it does not establish an interval or every protection transition.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An absent evidence source is unavailable, not an empty log. A supplied empty source has zero rows; metrics requiring both sources remain absent unless both are supplied.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Evaluation refuses malformed intervals and alert transitions, unknown terminal reasons, inconsistent protection timestamps, overlapping same-address truth windows, more than 100,000 rows per source, or aggregate pairwise work over 10,000,000 comparisons. Work is checked with overflow-safe arithmetic before pairwise processing, charging all three hazard-alert passes and all unordered hazard-window comparisons. Accepted counts are independent of row order.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An airport's local east-north plane is a tangent plane about its reference point with the WGS-84 local scales and a curvature term. It is defined on the disc within 20 km of the origin, for an origin up to 80 degrees of latitude; a point outside the disc, a non-finite point or an origin outside those limits gives no position. On the disc a point's distance from the origin differs from the geodesic distance by at most 1.5 m, the plane error bound: test `plane_error_against_geodesic_is_within_the_stated_bound`, 11 latitudes to 80 degrees, 72 bearings, out to the edge (worst 1.05 m, at 80 degrees and 20 km). The distance between two points on the disc differs from the geodesic by at most twice the bound: test `plane_distance_between_two_points_against_geodesic_is_within_twice_the_bound`, 2,800 random pairs (worst 1.90 m). These are measured bounds on the cases tested, not proved ones.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A runway is built from the published length, width, alignment, end coordinates, displaced-threshold coordinates and declared distances. It keeps each physical end and each landing threshold apart, and the rectangle is the one between the physical ends at the published width (tests on KMDW 04L/22R, displaced at both ends, and on KAUS 18L/36R and KSFO 10L/28R, from the NASR 2026-10-29 values).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Per OA-ASP-067, an end with a displacement and no NASR displaced coordinate takes its landing threshold from the CIFP record and is marked as such; with no CIFP threshold the runway is refused. Where NASR has no end coordinate, the CIFP threshold is taken as the physical end only when the published displacement is exactly zero; with an unknown displacement the runway is refused. An end with both a NASR displaced coordinate and a CIFP threshold is refused when they lie more than 30 m apart, because one of them is wrong and nothing here can tell which.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A runway is refused, and counted under its own one of 16 reasons, when its width is missing, zero or over 500 ft, its length is missing, an end name is bad, a displacement is negative or not finite, a physical end or landing threshold is missing, a displaced coordinate has no displacement length to check it against, a coordinate is invalid or outside the plane, or the ends are under 1 m apart. Nothing is guessed.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A runway is refused when the published length and the distance between the physical ends differ by more than 60 m, the published alignment and the azimuth between the ends by more than 2 degrees, a published displacement and the measured one by more than 30 m, or a threshold lies more than 15 m off the line between the ends or outside the runway (tests include a threshold past the far end, and one 25 m behind the near end).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The occupancy regions are the rectangle, an approach area for each end measured outward from the landing threshold (1,500 m long, 100 m wider than the runway on each side) and a departure area beyond each physical end (1,000 m long, 50 m wider on each side). These dimensions are development values, not FAA values. The test `every_edge_of_every_region_at_the_interval_ends` probes each of the four edges of all five regions on the edge, inside, and outside by the margin and just past it, and the KMDW test checks the hand-worked interval ends.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: `occupies` reports whether a target touches the rectangle, either approach area or either departure area, with its position widened by its 95 % radius plus the 1.5 m plane error bound and a 1e-6 m rounding pad. A non-finite position or radius, negative radius, coordinate beyond 1e9 m, non-finite runway geometry, or inconsistent published and derived runway widths counts as occupying every region and is marked unknown. Every comparison is written so that a NaN reads as touching. Tests `unknown_position_or_radius_occupies_everything`, `a_runway_with_a_non_finite_number_never_clears_a_target`, `a_torn_finite_width_change_is_unknown_while_a_coherent_geometry_change_can_clear` and `real_coordinates_run_end_to_end_through_the_plane_and_the_test` (KMDW, from latitude and longitude).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: Raising the radius never removes a region from the result. Tested by a sweep of radii at six positions (`a_larger_radius_only_adds_occupancy`) and by OA-RWY-009.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For finite radii 0 <= r1 <= r2, a target that occupies a region at r1 occupies it at r2, and the runway-axis coordinates do not depend on the radius. Tested, not proved: on 30,000 random runways at any heading, positions within 1e9 m and radii up to 1e9 m, through `occupies` itself (`a_larger_radius_never_clears_a_region_for_random_runways_positions_and_radii`).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A non-finite, negative or beyond-1e9 m position or radius occupies every region and is marked unknown, and so does every position and radius on a runway with any non-finite number. Tested, not proved: at the edge values, and on 30,000 random runways with a position, a radius or one of the runway's 16 numbers set to NaN, infinity or beyond the limit (`a_position_radius_or_runway_that_is_not_known_occupies_every_region_for_random_runways`).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For every runway of the kind `build_runway` makes and every finite radius of at least zero, a target whose coordinates in the runway axes lie inside the rectangle touches it. Tested, not proved: 1e-6 m inside the edges and on the edges themselves with a radius above zero (`a_target_inside_the_runway_rectangle_touches_it_at_every_radius`), and on 30,000 random runways (`a_target_inside_a_random_runway_rectangle_touches_it_at_every_radius`).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: For every runway of the kind `build_runway` makes (finite geometry within 1e9 m, axis components within [-1, 1]) and every position and radius, any `f64` bit pattern included, `occupies` returns without panic, and for a known position the coordinates in the runway axes are finite and under 1e10 m. Proved with Kani (`occupies_never_panics`). The proof checks panics and those assertions; it does not run a separate float-overflow check.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The conversion from degrees to the local plane gives no position for a non-finite input, and any position it gives is finite, within 20 km on each axis and inside the extent's disc. Tested, not proved: on 30,000 random origins and points, up to `f64::MAX`, NaN and infinity included (`a_point_in_the_local_plane_is_finite_and_inside_the_extent_or_refused_for_random_origins_and_points`).

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: An interval between consecutive times of a feed over 600 s is an excluded interval (P-007), not damage by itself; exactly 600 s is not over.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A window with no message in a feed is damaged.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: This evaluates saved or synthetic evidence and has no direct runtime control effect.
non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: At most 1,000 intervals over 600 s are listed; the rest are counted and make the window damaged.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: A frame the reader finds damaged is counted by kind, never skipped silently.

non_safety_requirement_assessments.register_clause: The opt-in raw-only replay CLI writes and verifies a versioned restart witness binding exact adaptation and clip bytes, declared receipt basis, effective render/raw settings, frame count, and ordered frame indexes, nanosecond timestamps and pixel hashes. Verification checks the bounded witness checksum and metadata before creating output, then compares each recomputed frame before publishing it; a mismatch refuses further frames and identifies that earlier matching frames may already exist. A successful restart reproduces the same ordered hashes. The witness is limited to 1,000,000 bytes and 10,000 frames; unknown fields, partial lists and incorrect times are refused. Lossy replay cannot produce or pass a witness even with `--allow-loss`. Output never overwrites an existing witness or partial: a recovery copy is synced under an exclusive partial name before a distinct final file is exclusively created and synced. The complete recovery copy remains after success; publication deletes neither file. Interrupted final publication may leave an incomplete final name, which strict verification refuses; the complete partial can be explicitly selected for verification. No hard-link exception weakens the shared sealed-data guard. SHA-256 is integrity evidence, not authentication. Replay starts from the beginning; this feature neither restores process state nor provides supervision or failover.

CF=6's body uses the DF17 message formats and is decoded under OA-MODE-004; its AA field is not promoted to ICAO-24 by this decoder. This is not address registration validation.

DF18 CF=4 is identified as reserved TIS-B management, but its body remains uninterpreted.

This one-frame API does not establish the altitude's datum/source. Q=0 (100-foot Mode C/Gillham encoding) is retained raw and explicitly marked unsupported; no altitude is fabricated. TC 20–22 and other CF families remain uninterpreted for altitude.

unclassified_requirement_policy.rationale: Every active register ID has an explicit safety, non-safety, or unresolved function assessment. Unresolved IDs remain an open engineering question rather than being silently assigned a function.

open_items.detail: Complete the system/function hazard analysis with facility context, operational barriers, probability allocation, and approved severity before assigning assurance levels.
Trace references identify existing source tests or proofs; this log does not establish that they passed in a qualification run or provide independent verification.

hazards.cause: A facility, runway, route, procedure, airspace, or adaptation record is misdecoded, incomplete, or associated with the wrong source.
hazards.effect: A route, boundary, or facility constraint may be misplaced or missing from downstream display and warning functions.
hazards.severity_rationale: Incorrect navigation or airspace information can contribute to unsafe routing or terrain exposure; facility adaptation is not approved here.

safety_requirement_assessments.rationale: Engineering safety candidate: missing, corrupt, unsupported, or wrong-facility preset loading can change conflict-alert behavior. The runtime regression verifies a synthetic issued v3 package, the independent pin, exact typed minima and policy loading before `ca_check`, then shows those minima govern an ordinary CA cycle. The fixture is schema-generated synthetic metadata with empty tables; this does not establish issuer authentication, operational approval, or recorded-rate performance.

Engineering safety candidate: issuing a CA preset with the wrong facility, malformed geometry or policy, or damaged component identity could feed incorrect warning configuration. The shared parser and exact read-back, component, and facility checks constrain byte and identity errors, but do not authenticate the issuer or establish operational approval. The directly tagged test verifies preset issuance/read-back and identity damage; it does not establish operational validity.
